power.title: Charter Order
power.flavour: You stamp an order with Geneva's seal. Any office here must obey it.

law.title: Charter Renewal Act
law.flavour: Earth's law and its promise of rescue, signed for ten more years.

picks.title: Home and Hull
picks.flavour: Every clock shows Earth time next to the Mars day.

picks.title: Charter Clerks
picks.flavour: Petitions are filed in three copies and answered within the week.

picks.title: Rescue Guarantee
picks.flavour: Earth's Charter office remembers who stayed loyal.

power.title: Exchange Deal
power.flavour: A handshake and real coffee in the arcade. The merchants trade what you need.

law.title: Concession Charter
law.flavour: Air, ice and landing pads, all priced and privately owned.

picks.title: Ice Futures
picks.flavour: Ice prices tick on the trading boards all shift long.

picks.title: Merchant Lobby
picks.flavour: Merchant families' agents wait in every Dome 1 corridor.

picks.title: Tax Holiday
picks.flavour: Merchants pay less tax and trade more.

power.title: Dustline Hour
power.flavour: The pirate radio and the drums carry your words to every tube block.

law.title: Arcadian Self-Government Act
law.flavour: The Mars-born run their own home. Only they decide who comes in.

picks.title: Pressure Holds
picks.flavour: The Mars-born greeting, 'Pressure holds', becomes a vow.

picks.title: Mars Calendar
picks.flavour: The colony broadcast now counts only Mars days.

picks.title: Basalt Galleries
picks.flavour: Mars-born carvers cut deeper spirals into the lava tube walls.

power.title: Union Show of Hands
power.flavour: The union hall votes with raised orange gloves to back your cause.

law.title: Supply Councils Act
law.flavour: Air, water and food, shared out by the workers who make them.

picks.title: Shift Councils
picks.flavour: Every work crew elects a council and reports each shift.

picks.title: Common Stock
picks.flavour: The ice belongs to everyone, kept in one common store.

picks.title: Pump-Beat Songs
picks.flavour: Union work songs to the airlock pump beat, all night long.

power.title: Shift-Change Briefing
power.flavour: Engineers read every air and water reserve aloud. You draw on what they find.

law.title: Reserves First Act
law.flavour: Politics stops where the reserve gauges start.

picks.title: Certified Minimum
picks.flavour: Every power load must be justified on the reserve board.

picks.title: Reserve Board
picks.flavour: Engineers' trust changes slowly, up or down.

picks.title: Green Line
picks.flavour: The reserves stay above the safe line, and faith follows.

centreLaws.title: Concord of the Landing
centreLaws.flavour: One colony, two clocks, and every faction with a seat.

centreLaws.title: Joint Supply Board
centreLaws.flavour: Engineers, work crews and Assembly members read one gauge together.

iron.title: Lock Codes
iron.flavour: Every public airlock answers to Dome 1, the seat of government.

iron.title: Sedition Warrants
iron.flavour: Arrest warrants for sedition, signed in advance, stacked by the armoury.

iron.title: Police Paid First
iron.flavour: Officers are paid first, whatever the reserves say.

open.title: Live Assembly
open.flavour: Every Assembly session is broadcast live and uncut.

open.title: Petition Box
open.flavour: Settlers' petitions are read aloud in the Assembly Hall.

open.title: Open Reserve Log
open.flavour: Anyone can read the air and water gauges now.

centre.title: Shared Key
centre.flavour: No one group holds the whole key.

centre.title: Broker's Table
centre.flavour: Deals are struck before a bill reaches the Assembly floor.

centre.title: Two Clocks
centre.flavour: Earth time and Mars time, kept side by side.

iron.title: Lava Tube Curfew
iron.flavour: The airlocks into the lava tube close at 22:00.

iron.title: Sedition Sweep
iron.flavour: Organisers are arrested before the dawn shift.

open.title: Uncut Channel
open.flavour: The censors' desk in Dome 1 shuts down. The broadcast runs uncut.

open.title: Pressure Day Pardons
open.flavour: The 41 protesters walk free from the Dome 1 cells.

mca.title: Life-Support Subsidy
mca.flavour: Earth pays for the air, and Earth watches how it is spent.

hac.title: Company Loan
hac.flavour: Credit from Helion-Ares, on the company's terms.

upa.title: Overland Convoy
upa.flavour: Fourteen rovers arrive from the rival colony to the west.

aco.title: Constabulary Over Your Head
aco.question: The Commandant wants a free hand in the tube. Will you give it?
aco.body: Erebus Tube posts are emptying. Officers say Dome 1 is soft on Free Arcadia. The Commandant has drafted a cable to Geneva. 600 officers wait on your answer.

answers.text: Grant Erebus posts and a budget line
answers.sub: Permanent posts, own budget, Charter chain of command.

reasons.aco: Its own budget and the tube back under guard.
reasons.mca: A Charter service firmly in the governor's chain.
reasons.fam: Armed posts on its block doors.
reasons.cas: Police money voted without the Assembly.

answers.gripWhy: Armed posts made permanent in the tube.

answers.text: Fold lock security under Directorate codes
answers.sub: Engineers hold the codes; officers guard, not decide.

reasons.hsd: Locks run by its master systems at last.
reasons.aco: Stripped of its codes by engineers.
reasons.fam: Fewer officers deciding who passes.
reasons.mca: Charter police subordinated to a bureau.

hsd.title: Certified Minimum
hsd.question: The Directorate threatens certified-minimum operation. Will you yield the margins?
hsd.body: Control Ring, shift change. Non-life-support loads flagged for cutting. The Directorate will publish its margin log without your sign-off. The three-tone chime has sounded twice.

answers.text: Give the margin board binding force
answers.sub: No decree passes without a certified margin.

reasons.hsd: The final word on power and air.
reasons.cas: Margins locked away from elected members.
reasons.riw: Engineers set quotas with no union voice.
reasons.mca: Safe margins keep Geneva's floor intact.

answers.text: Refer the margins to Geneva's auditors
answers.sub: Charter auditors certify; the Directorate reports.

reasons.mca: Its auditors over colonial engineers.
reasons.hsd: Its certifications second-guessed from Earth.
reasons.cas: The Directorate finally answers to someone.
reasons.lme: Audits mean slower permits and loads.

lme.title: The Arcade Shuts
lme.question: The Exchange is hoarding sealant and credit. Will you buy it back?
lme.body: The arcade tickers are frozen. Sealant stock has vanished from the shelves. Exchange accounts are moving onto Helion-Ares books on Earth. The treasury has no lender left in the Domes.

answers.text: Cut levies and guarantee private decks
answers.sub: Levy cut, decks protected by Charter clause.

reasons.lme: Its decks safe and its levies down.
reasons.riw: Merchants rewarded for starving the halls.
reasons.hsd: Private decks stay outside the calorie plan.
reasons.hac: A market colony keeps its bonds sound.

answers.text: Requisition hoarded sealant stock
answers.sub: Shift crews open the stores; receipts, not payment.

reasons.lme: Confiscation of its stock, its red line.
reasons.riw: Hoarders made to share the common stock.
reasons.hsd: Sealant back where the domes need it.
reasons.hac: Private stock seized sets a bad precedent.

answers.gripWhy: Private stores opened by order.

cas.title: No Confidence
cas.question: The Assembly refuses the levy. Will you give it power or prorogue it?
cas.body: Motion of no confidence carried. The levy vote is withheld. A delegation is booked on the Geneva link. Fifty seats, and the Speaker counting every one.

answers.text: Hand the Assembly the levy outright
answers.sub: The levy and budget voted in the Assembly Hall.

reasons.cas: Real power over the levy at last.
reasons.fam: A step toward self-government.
reasons.mca: Charter authority handed to a colonial chamber.
reasons.hac: Bond service at the mercy of a vote.

answers.gripWhy: Power shared with the elected chamber.

answers.text: Prorogue the sitting under the Charter
answers.sub: Sittings suspended; levy set by Dome 1 decree.

reasons.cas: Its sittings suspended, its red line.
reasons.mca: Charter order restored over a rebel chamber.
reasons.aco: A clear chain without Assembly obstruction.
reasons.fam: Its allies in the chamber silenced.

answers.gripWhy: The elected Assembly suspended by decree.

riw.title: Tankers Stopped
riw.question: The tankers are stopped at Ice Field 7. Will you meet the crews?
riw.body: Ice Field 7 gate. Tankers parked nose to tail. Electrolysis halls on work-to-rule. Water and oxygen lines dropping. Raised gloves at every hatch.

answers.text: Concede the quota and dust inspectors
answers.sub: Quotas cut; union medics may halt a shift.

reasons.riw: Lower quotas and its own inspectors.
reasons.hac: Its contract quotas gutted by Dome 1.
reasons.hsd: Union medics halting shifts upsets schedules.
reasons.fam: Workers win against Earth contractors.

answers.text: Send Directorate crews into the halls
answers.sub: Certified operators replace strikers at the trains.

reasons.riw: Scabs in its halls.
reasons.hsd: Its plants back under certified hands.
reasons.aco: Order in the halls without a fight.
reasons.fam: Mars-born crews pushed aside.

answers.gripWhy: Strikers replaced under Directorate order.

fam.title: The Concourse Rises
fam.question: The Movement holds the relay tonight. Will you talk or ban?
fam.body: Habitat Channel relay taken for a night. Duct-drums down the Erebus Tube. The Mars-born told to refuse every roll and ration card. 11,400 listening.

answers.text: Open talks on Arcadian status
answers.sub: A table in Dome 1 for the block committees.

reasons.fam: Recognition of the Mars-born as a people.
reasons.cas: Self-government enters the agenda.
reasons.mca: Talks with secessionists set a precedent.
reasons.aco: Soft on the Movement; officers feel abandoned.

answers.gripWhy: Dissidents brought to the table.

answers.text: Ban the block committees outright
answers.sub: Committees dissolved, organisers detained.

reasons.fam: Its committees broken, its youth hunted.
reasons.aco: A firm order against the Movement.
reasons.mca: Sedition crushed under Charter law.
reasons.cas: A ban on organising touches every member.

answers.gripWhy: A political movement banned.

mca.title: Subsidy Frozen
mca.question: Geneva has frozen the subsidy. Will you bend to the Commissioner?
mca.body: Geneva link, delayed fourteen minutes. The monthly subsidy is frozen. Emergency powers suspended pending inquiry. The treasury loses ₵150M a month already.

answers.text: Pledge the roll and full reporting
answers.sub: Every Mars-born registered; every margin reported.

reasons.mca: The roll and the reports it demands.
reasons.fam: The roll is a leash on the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: Geneva's terms accepted without a vote.
reasons.hsd: Reporting keeps the floor sacred.

answers.text: Cover the gap with Exchange credit
answers.sub: Merchant loans replace Geneva's money.

reasons.lme: The colony now borrows from its families.
reasons.mca: Its leverage undercut by merchants.
reasons.hac: Credit markets in place of Geneva.
reasons.aco: Its pay depends on brokers now.

hac.title: Bond Called
hac.question: Helion-Ares calls the tranche. Will you pay their price?
hac.body: Earth court filing received. ₵1.2 billion called. Colony spares struck off the Window Fleet manifest. The sunburst wordmark comes down from the Pad Field gantry.

answers.text: Guarantee the tranche and export priority
answers.sub: Ice exports first to Helion-Ares; interest paid.

reasons.hac: Bonds serviced and ice exports secured.
reasons.riw: Its ice sold abroad again.
reasons.upa: Its ice leases pushed aside.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice mortgaged to Earth.

answers.text: Call their bluff; ice stays Arcadian
answers.sub: No guarantee; ice exports held at home.

reasons.hac: Repudiation talk; its bonds in danger.
reasons.fam: The ice stays with the colony.
reasons.cas: Debt brought under the colony's control.
reasons.lme: Credit with Earth collapses for merchants.

upa.title: West Door Closing
upa.question: Utopia recalls its technicians. Will you keep the western door open?
upa.body: Utopian technicians pack their kits. Overland spares convoys halted at the 3,800 km mark. A back channel to Free Arcadia is open.

answers.text: Sign a technician exchange with Utopia
answers.sub: Utopian engineers in the plants, Arcadians to Utopia.

reasons.upa: A foothold in Arcadia's plants.
reasons.hsd: Skilled hands for the electrolysis trains.
reasons.mca: A rival power inside the Charter colony.
reasons.hac: A competitor near its contracts.

answers.text: Close the overland route
answers.sub: No rovers past the crater rim.

reasons.upa: Shut out of Arcadia.
reasons.mca: No Utopian foothold on its watch.
reasons.aco: One frontier fewer to guard.
reasons.hsd: Spares cut off when margins are thin.

elections.title: Assembly Vote Called
elections.question: The Assembly wants a general vote. Will you hold it now?
elections.body: Fifty seats. The roll stands at 40,212. Booths in every dome and along the Erebus Tube. The Charter bench wants delay; the self-government bloc wants it this month.

answers.text: Hold the vote on schedule
answers.sub: Booths open in every dome and the tube.

reasons.cas: Its mandate renewed by the settlers.
reasons.fam: Mars-born votes count in the tube.
reasons.mca: A vote that may elect secessionists.
reasons.aco: Rallies and booths stretch its officers.

answers.gripWhy: A free vote across the colony.

answers.text: Delay it a year under the Charter
answers.sub: Emergency clause; sittings continue unelected.

reasons.cas: Its mandate stretched without consent.
reasons.mca: No risky vote before renewal.
reasons.aco: No rallies to police.
reasons.fam: Its chance at the booths stolen.

answers.gripWhy: An election postponed by decree.

elections.title: Vote Before the Fleet
elections.question: The settlers want a vote before the fleet. Will you allow it?
elections.body: The Window Fleet is months out. The Assembly asks for a fresh mandate first. Block committees offer tellers. The Directorate offers a certified roll.

answers.text: Hold it with block-committee tellers
answers.sub: Union and block tellers count every booth.

reasons.riw: Its members count the votes.
reasons.cas: A fresh mandate before the Reckoning.
reasons.hsd: Untrained tellers on certified systems.
reasons.mca: An uncertified count before renewal.

answers.gripWhy: An open vote counted by the street.

answers.text: Directorate certifies a restricted roll
answers.sub: Only certified-shift settlers vote this time.

reasons.cas: A rigged roll shrinks its electorate.
reasons.hsd: Its certification decides who counts.
reasons.fam: Mars-born youth struck off.
reasons.aco: A smaller, calmer polling day.

answers.gripWhy: A restricted, certified electorate.

history.title: Oath in Dome 1
history.question: Governor, whose words will you swear by in Dome 1?
history.body: Assembly Hall, 0900 Earth time. 40,212 on the roll, 11,400 Mars-born. Thirty years of Directorate rule end today. The Geneva link is live. Duct-drums sound in the tube.

answers.text: Swear on the Charter, Geneva watching
answers.sub: Earth law first; the Directorate answers to you.

reasons.mca: Its appointee swears its Charter before all.
reasons.aco: A clear chain of command up to Geneva.
reasons.hsd: Thirty years of engineering rule ended.
reasons.fam: An Earth oath over Arcadian ground.

answers.gripWhy: Charter authority asserted over every dome.

answers.text: Keep the Directorate's margin board binding
answers.sub: Your decrees pass the gauges first.

reasons.hsd: Its board keeps the final word on air.
reasons.mca: Geneva's governor bows to engineers.
reasons.cas: Margins stay closed to the Assembly.
reasons.aco: Order kept by people who know the plants.

answers.text: Add a pledge to the Mars-born
answers.sub: Arcadians named; self-government talks promised.

reasons.fam: Its people named in the governor's oath.
reasons.cas: Self-government finally on the table.
reasons.mca: A secession precedent in the first sentence.
reasons.aco: Soft words to the Movement on day one.

answers.gripWhy: A promise of shared power.

history.history: In history: Ilunga-Varga swore on the Charter in Dome 1 before a roll of 40,212, ending thirty years of Directorate rule.

history.title: First Margin Report
history.question: Oxygen sits at 186 days. Will you publish it as certified?
history.body: Quarterly margin report. Oxygen: 186 days against the Charter floor of 180. Water: 240 days. Six days of slack. Erebus brokers already quote air credits higher.

answers.text: Publish the certified log in full
answers.sub: Margins read aloud at every zero briefing.

reasons.hsd: Its certification stands public and untouched.
reasons.lme: Air-credit prices spike on the news.
reasons.mca: Geneva gets the honest figure it demands.
reasons.hac: Bond markets read six days as risk.

answers.text: Release it with an air-credit float
answers.sub: Brokers sell forward air to fund new stacks.

reasons.lme: A legal market in forward air.
reasons.hac: Private capital in the plants.
reasons.hsd: Air sold forward against its margins.
reasons.riw: Workers' air priced like Exchange goods.
reasons.fam: Air Is Ours, not the brokers'.

history.history: In history: The Directorate certified oxygen at 186 days against the 180-day floor, and water at 240 days.

history.title: Ice Field 7 Stops
history.question: Ice Field 7 has stopped. Whose side will you take, Governor?
history.body: Helion-Ares raised shift quotas 15 percent. 2,900 RIWU crews downed tools for 72 hours. Tankers idle at the field gate. Water reserve at 240 days and falling a day a day.

answers.text: Suspend the quota rise pending talks
answers.sub: Crews return under the old quota.

reasons.riw: The quota rise stopped by the strike.
reasons.hac: Its contract quotas overridden.
reasons.fam: A workers' victory echoes in the tube.
reasons.hsd: Talks delay tanker scheduling.

answers.text: Back the contract; pay strikebreaker bonuses
answers.sub: Exchange crews keep the tankers rolling.

reasons.hac: Its quotas defended, its ice moving.
reasons.lme: Bonus contracts for its crews.
reasons.riw: Scabs on its field.
reasons.fam: Earth money breaking Mars-born crews.

answers.text: Order arbitration under the Charter labour clause
answers.sub: Strikes past 72 hours become unlawful.

reasons.mca: Charter law settles colonial labour.
reasons.aco: A legal basis to clear the gates.
reasons.riw: Strike right capped by a Geneva clause.
reasons.cas: The Assembly left out of it.
reasons.hac: Arbitration likely favours the contract.

answers.gripWhy: Long strikes made unlawful.

history.history: In history: 2,900 RIWU crews stopped work at Ice Field 7 for 72 hours over the 15 percent quota rise.

history.title: Article 19 Warrant
history.question: Valdivia called to close the airlock. Will you sign the warrant?
history.body: Dustline broadcast, 2200. Ezra Valdivia, 27, told the Mars-born to close the airlock on Geneva. The Constabulary holds an Article 19 sedition warrant. Commandant Osei-Brandt waits on your signature.

answers.text: Sign the Article 19 sedition warrant
answers.sub: Valdivia detained; trial under Charter law.

reasons.aco: The ringleader in its cells.
reasons.mca: Sedition answered under its Charter.
reasons.fam: Its founder jailed for words.
reasons.cas: A broadcast is now a crime.

answers.gripWhy: A political leader jailed for a broadcast.

answers.text: Refuse; call it protected Arcadian speech
answers.sub: Valdivia stays free; the broadcast stands.

reasons.fam: Its founder free and its words lawful.
reasons.cas: Speech protected in the colony.
reasons.aco: Soft on the Movement; officers lose nerve.
reasons.mca: Secession talk tolerated by its governor.

answers.gripWhy: Sedition charges refused.

answers.text: Have the Directorate cut his relay
answers.sub: No arrest; Dustline loses its power feed.

reasons.hsd: The grid used as quiet control.
reasons.aco: No arrest; the street sees weakness.
reasons.fam: Its channel throttled by engineers.
reasons.mca: Sedition silenced without a martyr.
reasons.riw: Power cuts as a weapon; strikes next.

history.history: In history: The Constabulary detained Ezra Valdivia under Charter Article 19 for sedition after his broadcast.

history.title: Pressure Day
history.question: 6,000 fill the concourse. Will you clear them or hear them?
history.body: Erebus Tube concourse. 6,000 settlers, duct-drums, 'Air Is Ours' on every lock door. They demand Valdivia's release. Constabulary lines hold the Dome 1 locks.

answers.text: Receive a concourse delegation in Dome 1
answers.sub: Demands read into the record; no arrests.

reasons.fam: Its demands heard in Dome 1.
reasons.cas: Petitioners treated as citizens.
reasons.aco: Its lines stood down before a mob.
reasons.mca: Its governor negotiating with seditionists.

answers.gripWhy: Protesters received, not detained.

answers.text: Clear the concourse under the Charter lock code
answers.sub: Lock-safety order; organisers detained.

reasons.aco: Order in the tube, as it asked.
reasons.mca: Charter law enforced below the basalt.
reasons.fam: Its people detained on Pressure Day.
reasons.cas: Settlers arrested for petitioning.
reasons.riw: Its members among the detained.

answers.gripWhy: A rally cleared and organisers detained.

history.history: In history: 6,000 settlers filled the Erebus concourse demanding Valdivia's release; the Constabulary detained 41.

history.title: Dust Over Arcadia
history.question: Solar is down 40 percent. Whose load will you cut first?
history.body: Regional dust storm. Solar fields at 60 percent, 51 sols forecast. Oxygen slipping faster than six days a month. The margin board flashes amber.

answers.text: Directorate load-shed by certified priority
answers.sub: Life support first; shops and decks dim.

reasons.hsd: Its protocol governs the storm.
reasons.lme: Its shops dark for 51 sols.
reasons.cas: No vote on who goes dark.
reasons.mca: Margin protocol kept to the letter.

answers.gripWhy: Power rationed by Directorate order.

answers.text: Shift councils decide the load-share
answers.sub: Union crews ration power block by block.

reasons.riw: Its councils hold the switches.
reasons.fam: Blocks running their own power.
reasons.hsd: Untrained councils on its grid.
reasons.lme: Councils cut merchants first.
reasons.aco: Councils, not officers, run the blocks.

answers.gripWhy: Power handed to elected councils.

answers.text: Auction surplus power to the highest bidders
answers.sub: The Exchange buys backup; treasury takes the premium.

reasons.lme: Power for those who can pay.
reasons.hac: Market pricing in a crisis.
reasons.riw: Crews priced out of their own power.
reasons.fam: Air for the rich in a storm.
reasons.hsd: Margins bent by a price list.

history.history: In history: A regional dust storm cut solar output by 40 percent for 51 sols.

history.title: Train 3 Burns
history.question: Two operators dead in Train 3. Who will you let investigate?
history.body: Sabatier Train 3 fire. Two operators killed. Methane and water recovery down 30 percent. RIWU crews sing cycler laments at the hall door.

answers.text: Open a joint inquiry with union investigators
answers.sub: RIWU inspectors in the hall; findings published.

reasons.riw: Its own investigators for its own dead.
reasons.cas: A public inquiry the members can read.
reasons.hsd: Union men reading its logs.
reasons.hac: Its maintenance contract exposed.

answers.gripWhy: A public inquiry with outside investigators.

answers.text: Closed Directorate review, findings certified
answers.sub: Engineers investigate engineers; trains back first.

reasons.hsd: Its review, its findings, its trains.
reasons.mca: No scandal on the Geneva feeds.
reasons.riw: Its dead judged by those it blames.
reasons.fam: Another closed-door cover-up.

history.history: In history: A fire in Sabatier Train 3 killed two operators and cut methane and water recovery by 30 percent.

history.title: The Tranche Rolls
history.question: ₵1.2 billion falls due today. How will you meet Helion-Ares?
history.body: Bond tranche due: ₵1.2 billion. The treasury cannot repay it. Helion-Ares offers six months at 9 percent. The self-government bloc says Earth debt is not Arcadian debt.

answers.text: Roll it over at 9 percent
answers.sub: Six months; about ₵9M a month interest.

reasons.lme: Credit with Earth stays open.
reasons.cas: Debt rolled without a levy vote.
reasons.fam: Arcadia keeps paying Earth bondholders.
reasons.riw: Interest paid from its ice.

answers.text: Declare it colonial debt, not Arcadian
answers.sub: Repudiation talk; interest paused.

reasons.fam: Earth's debt is not Arcadia's.
reasons.cas: Debt brought before the colony.
reasons.hac: Its bonds repudiated in all but name.
reasons.mca: A Charter colony defaulting on Earth.
reasons.lme: Merchant credit dries up.

answers.text: Pay in common-stock ice, no export rights
answers.sub: Settle in tonnes, not field concessions.

reasons.riw: Ice stays common, no export grab.
reasons.upa: Ice slips off Helion-Ares's books.
reasons.hac: Paid in ice, not rights.
reasons.hsd: Reserve ice traded away.
reasons.lme: No export trade for merchants.

history.history: In history: Helion-Ares rolled over the ₵1.2 billion tranche for six months at 9 percent.

reasons.hac: A competing supplier at its gate.

answers.sub: Geneva clears every crate; Utopians logged.

reasons.mca: Its customs over every crate.
reasons.aco: Foreigners logged at its gate.
reasons.upa: Its gift treated as contraband.
reasons.hsd: Spares delayed in customs.

history.history: In history: A Utopia Planitia convoy of 14 rovers arrived after 3,800 km with 40 tonnes of electrolysis spares.

history.title: Marines Will Sail

history.body: The Charter Authority announces a battalion of 400 Charter Marines aboard the Window Fleet. Free Arcadia calls it an invasion. Utopia Planitia watches from the west.

reasons.aco: It fears being replaced by Marines.
reasons.fam: An invasion force, its red line.
reasons.upa: Marines on its doorstep.

answers.gripWhy: Earth troops invited to the colony.

answers.sub: Formal objection on the Geneva link.

reasons.fam: The governor refuses Earth's soldiers.

reasons.mca: Its governor resisting its own troops.
reasons.aco: No backup coming for its officers.

answers.sub: Spares and trade goods instead of soldiers.

reasons.lme: More paying cargo on the fleet.
reasons.hac: Its slots stay full and profitable.
reasons.mca: Its battalion haggled away.
reasons.aco: Its reinforcement traded for cargo.

history.history: In history: The Charter Authority announced that 400 Charter Marines would sail with the Window Fleet.

history.title: Reactor Two Scrams
history.question: Domes 2 to 5 face 22 sols dark. Who will you keep lit?
history.body: Reactor Two scrammed at 0412. A 22-sol brownout across Domes 2 to 5. Electrolysis halls on reserve feeds. The arcade's tickers have gone blank.

answers.text: Halls and homes first; councils ration
answers.sub: Crews share power by block, the arcade dark.

reasons.riw: Its councils keep halls and homes lit.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks served before the arcade.
reasons.lme: Its arcade dark for 22 sols.
reasons.hsd: Councils overriding its load plan.
reasons.hac: Export processing halted.

answers.text: Lease Exchange generators at market rate
answers.sub: Private fuel cells, billed to the treasury.

reasons.lme: Paid for its generators.
reasons.hac: Market keeps the plants running.
reasons.riw: Paying the Exchange for its own air.
reasons.fam: Merchants profit from the dark.

history.history: In history: Reactor Two scrammed, and a 22-sol brownout fell across Domes 2 to 5.

history.title: Bill at First Reading
history.question: The Self-Government Bill passed 31 to 19. Will you let it stand?
history.body: Colonial Assembly, first reading: 31 for, 19 against. 26 needed. The Charter bench walked out. Duct-drums in the gallery.

answers.text: Let it stand; recognise the vote
answers.sub: No Charter veto at first reading.

reasons.cas: Its bill stands untouched.
reasons.fam: Self-government one reading closer.
reasons.mca: Secession advancing unvetoed.
reasons.aco: Its chain to Geneva fraying.

answers.gripWhy: An elected vote respected.

answers.text: Demand a union allocation clause in it
answers.sub: Self-government only with RIWU board seats.

reasons.riw: Its seat written into the new order.
reasons.fam: Workers and Mars-born together.
reasons.lme: Union seats over its trade.
reasons.hac: Councils over its ice plant.
reasons.cas: Its bill rewritten from Dome 1.

history.history: In history: The Colonial Assembly passed the Self-Government Bill's first reading 31 to 19.

Win Free Arcadia up to 40 or more.

situations.title: Six Days to Spare
situations.question: Governor, will you ration air in every dome or cut ice shifts?
situations.body: The Directorate, the colony's engineers, report oxygen at 186 days. The Charter's legal minimum is 180. The reserve falls five to six days a month. They offer two cuts: 8 percent less air and power everywhere, or fewer union shifts at Ice Field 7.

answers.text: Cut air and power 8 percent everywhere.
answers.sub: Every dome breathes less. The reserve lasts longer.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, and our engineers are obeyed.
reasons.riw: The cut falls on everyone, not only our crews.
reasons.lme: Less power dims the arcade and cuts our trading hours.
reasons.cas: A ration imposed without one vote in our chamber.
reasons.mca: A governor who guards the legal minimum keeps Geneva calm.

answers.gripWhy: Rationing by order, enforced at every meter.

answers.text: Cut Ice Field 7 shifts; keep the arcade lit.
answers.sub: Fewer union shifts. The shops keep full power.

reasons.lme: Our shops stay open while the cut lands elsewhere.
reasons.riw: Our crews lose pay so the arcade keeps its lights.
reasons.hsd: Fewer shifts mean less load on the oxygen plants.
reasons.fam: Tube families pay for the merchants' comfort again.
reasons.hac: Fewer shifts mean fewer tankers of ice to export.

answers.text: Let elected work councils share out the cut.
answers.sub: Crews and tube blocks decide where the 8 percent falls.

reasons.riw: Those who make the air decide how it is shared.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks finally get a say over their own air.
reasons.hsd: Air handed to amateurs who cannot read a gauge.
reasons.aco: Councils over the meters weaken our chain of command.
reasons.mca: Geneva does not accept union councils over life support.

answers.gripWhy: Control of air passes from engineers to elected councils.

situations.title: Earth Flags in the Tube
situations.question: Will you raise the Charter flag everywhere and swear the Constabulary to it?
situations.body: Geneva's swearing-in order came over the link. It wants the blue Charter flag in every dome, the lava tube too. The Constabulary, the colony police, would swear to the Charter, not the Directorate. Dustline, the pirate radio, says any flag in the tube comes down by night.

answers.text: Fly the flags everywhere; swear the Constabulary in.
answers.sub: Charter oath in Dome 1. Blue flags down the tube.

reasons.mca: The Charter's rule is visible in every dome.
reasons.aco: A clear chain of command straight up to Geneva.
reasons.fam: Earth flags in our tube are an occupier's flags.
reasons.hsd: Thirty years of our command ended by one oath.
reasons.cas: The governor takes orders from Geneva, not our chamber.

answers.gripWhy: Police sworn to Earth, and flags guarded in the tube.

answers.text: Keep Earth flags out of the tube.
answers.sub: Charter flags fly in Domes 1 to 5 only.

reasons.fam: The tube stays ours, under the two moons.
reasons.cas: A governor who listens to our self-government bloc.
reasons.mca: An order half obeyed invites secession.
reasons.aco: We are told to leave the tube to the separatists.

answers.text: Leave the police oath with the Directorate.
answers.sub: The Constabulary still answers to the engineers.

reasons.hsd: Security stays tied to the plants it protects.
reasons.upa: Geneva's hold on the Domes loosens a notch.
reasons.mca: The governor refuses the first order Geneva sends.
reasons.aco: We stay under engineers instead of the Charter.
reasons.fam: No oath to Earth is sworn over our heads.

situations.title: Air Sold Twice
situations.question: Will you tax the tube's air-credit market or let police raid it?
situations.body: Air credits are ration slips for air. In the Erebus Tube, the main lava tube, stalls resell them for two to three times the ration price. Chair Castellanos-Abe of the Merchants' Exchange wants the trade licensed and taxed. Constabulary officers have raided the stalls twice this quarter.

answers.text: License the air-credit trade and tax it.
answers.sub: Stalls register, brokers pay, the treasury gains.

reasons.lme: Our brokers trade in the open, with legal papers.
reasons.hac: Priced air is a market our bondholders understand.
reasons.riw: Air we make is sold back to us at triple price.
reasons.fam: Tube families now pay legal prices for their own air.
reasons.aco: Our raids become illegal, and the stalls laugh at us.

answers.text: Raid the stalls under Charter ration law.
answers.sub: Credits seized, brokers fined, stalls shut.

reasons.aco: Order in the tube, and our officers backed.
reasons.mca: Charter ration law means what it says.
reasons.lme: Our members' stock seized by police at night.
reasons.fam: Police kicking in stalls in our blocks again.

answers.gripWhy: Armed officers raid tube stalls at night.

situations.title: The Edited Feed
situations.question: Will you let Assembly sittings run uncut on the Habitat Channel?
situations.body: The Habitat Channel is the colony's broadcast network. Your office edits every Assembly broadcast before it airs. The self-government bloc and Free Arcadia, the independence movement, want the feed live and whole. Last week's edit cut four minutes of the Speaker's tax speech.

answers.text: Run every sitting live and uncut.
answers.sub: No more edits. The chamber speaks to every dome.

reasons.cas: Our words reach the settlers whole.
reasons.fam: Self-government speeches heard in every tube block.
reasons.lme: Our bench's tax fights get a public stage.
reasons.mca: Secession talk broadcast live under Charter authority.
reasons.aco: Live agitation on screen stirs up the tube.

answers.gripWhy: You give up control of the broadcast.

answers.text: Keep editing under Charter broadcast rules.
answers.sub: Your office still cuts the feed before it airs.

reasons.mca: No secession speeches on a Charter channel.
reasons.aco: Fewer slogans on screen, fewer at the locks.
reasons.cas: Our sittings censored by the governor's office.
reasons.fam: The pirate Dustline will carry whatever Dome 1 cuts.

answers.gripWhy: You keep censoring the chamber.

situations.title: Dust in the Lungs
situations.question: Will you give union inspectors the power to stop a shift?
situations.body: Ice Field 7 has 140 lung cases. Toxic perchlorate dust gets past the suit seals. The RIWU, the ice workers' union, wants its own medical inspectors. They could halt any shift. Helion-Ares, the Earth company running the ice contracts, says every halted shift loses a tanker.

answers.text: Appoint union inspectors who can halt shifts.
answers.sub: Union doctors walk the field with the power to stop work.

reasons.riw: Our own people decide when the dust is too thick.
reasons.fam: Mars-born crews protected by their own people.
reasons.hac: Our quotas now hang on a union doctor's whim.
reasons.hsd: Shifts halted with no regard for the reserves.
reasons.lme: Ice deliveries become unreliable for our contracts.

answers.text: Give the inspections to Dr. Begić's medical service.
answers.sub: Directorate doctors check suits. Halts need engineers' approval.

reasons.hsd: Certified staff, with halts weighed against the reserves.
reasons.mca: The Charter medical service keeps its authority.
reasons.hac: The fields keep running unless the engineers agree.
reasons.riw: The Directorate inspects itself while our lungs fill.

answers.text: Make Helion-Ares pay into a compensation fund.
answers.sub: Sick crews get paid. Quotas stay as they are.

reasons.hac: We pay for lungs on top of the quota.
reasons.lme: A paid settlement keeps the fields and trade moving.
reasons.riw: Money for the sick, though the dust stays.
reasons.cas: A deal our chamber can vote on and claim.

situations.title: The Price of Six Months
situations.question: Will you trade sole ice export rights to delay the debt payment?
situations.body: A ₵1.2 billion bond payment falls due in October. The treasury holds ₵2.4 billion and loses ₵150M a month. Katharina Sørlie-Tan, head of Helion-Ares, offers six more months at 9 percent. Her price: sole rights to export the colony's ice.

answers.text: Give Helion-Ares sole export rights.
answers.sub: The debt is delayed. Every tonne leaves on their ships.

reasons.hac: Bonds paid and the ice trade locked up.
reasons.lme: Stable credit and cargo work for the arcade.
reasons.upa: Utopia is shut out of Arcadian ice.
reasons.riw: Our ice sold abroad by the company that sets quotas.
reasons.fam: Arcadia's ice signed away to an Earth corporation.

answers.text: Refuse; Arcadian ice stays Arcadian.
answers.sub: No monopoly. The money must be found elsewhere.

reasons.fam: The colony keeps its ice and its future.
reasons.cas: The ice stays a matter for our chamber.
reasons.upa: The door to an ice lease stays open.
reasons.hac: Our bonds left hanging after a refusal.
reasons.lme: Credit tightens while the bondholders are angry.

situations.title: The Citizenship Line
situations.question: Will you enforce Geneva's new roll on Mars-born families?
situations.body: Geneva wants every Mars-born child listed on the settler roll as an Earth citizen. Clerks sit in Dome 1 and the Erebus concourse. Free Arcadia's block committees tell families not to register. By day three, 212 forms were filed for 11,400 Mars-born.

answers.text: No registration, no ration card.
answers.sub: No roll entry, no card. Officers back the clerks.

reasons.mca: Every Mars-born on the roll as an Earth citizen.
reasons.aco: A full roll lets us know who lives in the tube.
reasons.fam: Air held hostage to a leash from Geneva.
reasons.cas: Forced registration without one Assembly vote.
reasons.riw: Our members' families threatened through their rations.

answers.gripWhy: Rations become a lever to force registration.

answers.text: List the Mars-born as Arcadians, not Earth citizens.
answers.sub: A colony roll with no Earth citizenship for Geneva.

reasons.fam: The governor writes our people down as Arcadians.
reasons.cas: A colony roll our chamber can own.
reasons.mca: The governor defies the Charter on citizenship itself.
reasons.aco: We swore to a Charter the governor now ignores.

answers.text: Let block committees count heads, without citizenship.
answers.sub: Work and block lists, used for rations only.

reasons.riw: Our committees, not Geneva's clerks, hold the lists.
reasons.fam: Counted for air, never for Earth.
reasons.hsd: An accurate headcount for the ration tables.
reasons.mca: Geneva's roll replaced by union lists.
reasons.aco: Committees keep records the police cannot see.

situations.title: Nine Private Decks
situations.question: Will you seize the merchants' greenhouse decks for the shared food plan?
situations.body: The dust storm season is five months away. Exchange merchant families run nine private greenhouse decks in Dome 2. The Directorate wants their crops in the common food plan. Chair Castellanos-Abe calls seizure theft.

answers.text: Seize the decks for the food plan.
answers.sub: Directorate planners run the harvest from tomorrow.

reasons.hsd: Every calorie counted before the storm hits.
reasons.riw: Private decks feed everyone, not only the rich.
reasons.upa: A planned colony is one we can deal with.
reasons.lme: Seizing our decks crosses our red line.
reasons.hac: Private property seized; our investors grow nervous.

answers.gripWhy: Private decks taken by order.

answers.text: Buy their surplus at market price.
answers.sub: The treasury pays. The decks stay private.

reasons.lme: Our harvest sells at a fair price.
reasons.hac: Property respected, even before a storm.
reasons.hsd: Food at market prices wrecks our plan.
reasons.riw: Public money flows to deck owners.

answers.text: Hand the decks to union greenhouse crews.
answers.sub: Crews run them as shared property.

reasons.riw: The decks go to those who grow the food.
reasons.fam: Food for the tube, out of merchant hands.
reasons.lme: Our decks handed to the union outright.
reasons.hac: Seizure today, our ice plant tomorrow.
reasons.aco: Union crews holding decks the Charter calls private.

situations.title: Mars Geography Lessons
situations.question: Will you replace the Earth syllabus with an Arcadian one?
situations.body: Schools still teach Earth geography and Concord civics. The Concord is Earth's world government. Mars-born teachers have written a course on Arcadian history and Mars geography. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau objects from Geneva. About 4,000 pupils start next term.

answers.text: Adopt the Arcadian course this term.
answers.sub: Mars time, local rock and Arcadia's history. Earth civics dropped.

reasons.fam: Our children learn they are a people.
reasons.cas: Our self-government bloc wins its first real reform.
reasons.mca: A generation schooled for secession on our subsidy.
reasons.aco: The schools raise the next armed Pressure Cells.

answers.text: Keep the Concord syllabus and Earth exams.
answers.sub: Earth certificates stay valid if pupils return to Earth.

reasons.mca: Mars-born children stay Concord citizens at heart.
reasons.aco: Order begins with what children are taught.
reasons.fam: Our children taught about a planet they will never see.
reasons.cas: The governor overrules the teachers and our chamber.

situations.title: One Shift to Answer
situations.question: The ice crews walk out next shift. Whose side will you take?
situations.body: Helion-Ares raised Ice Field 7 work quotas by 15 percent. The union voted a 72-hour stoppage by raised gloves. Its leader, Kamau-Quispe, gave you one shift to answer. The ice tankers feed the water reserve, now at 240 days.

answers.text: Order Helion-Ares to freeze the quota rise
answers.sub: Quotas go back to the old rate. Crews stay on shift.

reasons.riw: The quota falls without a single lost shift.
reasons.hac: A governor rewriting our contracts threatens every bond.
reasons.lme: Ice costs rise and we merchants pay the gap.
reasons.hsd: Tankers keep running and the water reserve holds.
reasons.fam: Geneva's governor bending to Arcadian hands is a start.

answers.text: Back the quota rise and dock strikers' pay
answers.sub: The 15 percent stands. Strikers lose their shift pay.

reasons.hac: Our contract holds and the bondholders see a firm hand.
reasons.lme: Export volume keeps the arcade's credit open.
reasons.riw: Docking pay for lung-burned crews is open war.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice dug harder for Earth's bondholders.
reasons.hsd: A stoppage now would drain the water reserve.

answers.text: Send police to keep the tankers rolling
answers.sub: Officers escort tanker crews past any picket line.
answers.gripWhy: Armed officers guard the ice routes against a union.

reasons.aco: Charter order on the ice routes, under our command.
reasons.mca: Charter law keeps the colony's water flowing.
reasons.riw: Armed police on the fields is our red line.
reasons.cas: Armed escorts, and our chamber was not even asked.
reasons.hac: The tankers move and our shipments leave on time.

situations.title: Machines from the West
situations.question: Director Wen offers oxygen machines. Will you sell Utopia your ice?
situations.body: Utopia Planitia is a rival state-run settlement 3,800 km west. It offers machines that split water into oxygen. The price is 600 tonnes of ice a year. Director Wen also wants an office in the Domes. Helion-Ares claims that ice for export. Oxygen sits near the 180-day minimum.

answers.text: Take the machines and ship 600 tonnes
answers.sub: Utopian machines in the plants. A Utopian office opens.

reasons.upa: Ice, a foothold in the Domes, and Geneva's grip loosened.
reasons.hsd: New machines lift the oxygen reserve off the floor.
reasons.hac: Our export claims cut in half by a rival state.
reasons.mca: A Utopian office in a Charter colony sets a precedent.
reasons.riw: More machines mean fewer forced shifts in the halls.

answers.text: Refuse and honour Helion-Ares export claims
answers.sub: Every tonne stays on the company's contract books.

reasons.hac: The governor respects contracts. Our bonds stay safe.
reasons.lme: The company's cargo space keeps our trade alive.
reasons.upa: Arcadia chooses an Earth company over its neighbour.
reasons.hsd: Our plants go on without the machines they need.

answers.text: Send the offer to Geneva to decide
answers.sub: Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau rules. Months pass waiting on Earth.

reasons.mca: Foreign deals belong to the Charter Authority.
reasons.aco: The chain of command runs to Geneva, as it should.
reasons.upa: Geneva's answer is already known. Our offer dies.
reasons.hsd: The reserves cannot wait on Geneva's delay.
reasons.cas: Arcadia's ice is decided in Geneva again.

situations.title: Air Is Ours
situations.question: Will you post police at the tube locks for good?
situations.body: 'Air Is Ours' appeared overnight on every lock door in Free Arcadia's districts. Commandant Osei-Brandt asks for permanent police posts in the Erebus Tube concourse. Drum circles beat on old ducts under the rock galleries.

answers.text: Set up permanent posts in the concourse
answers.sub: Officers on every shift at the Erebus Tube locks.
answers.gripWhy: Standing police watch over the Mars-born districts.

reasons.aco: The tube is held. We own the locks again.
reasons.mca: Charter rule visible where it is most defied.
reasons.fam: Police occupying our own concourse.
reasons.cas: Policing tube voters costs our chamber their trust.
reasons.lme: A quieter concourse means safer stalls for our trade.

answers.text: Let tube block committees scrub the doors
answers.sub: Residents watch their own locks. No new posts.
answers.gripWhy: The Mars-born police their own districts.

reasons.fam: Dome 1 recognises our committees in all but name.
reasons.cas: Local self-rule is our chamber's own argument.
reasons.aco: The locks handed to Free Arcadia's own committees.
reasons.mca: Answering graffiti with concessions invites worse.

situations.title: Fees at the Pads
situations.question: Will you let the Exchange charge every ship at the landing pads?
situations.body: The Pad Field, where ships land, earns the colony nothing. The Merchants' Exchange and Helion-Ares want to run it for profit. Utopian rovers and Charter ships alike would pay a landing fee. The treasury loses ₵150M a month.

answers.text: Give the pads to the Exchange and Helion-Ares
answers.sub: Private operators charge every ship. The treasury takes a share.

reasons.lme: The pads become profit for the Exchange families.
reasons.hac: Our cargo flows through gates we co-own.
reasons.upa: Our convoys pay fees at a company tollbooth.
reasons.mca: Charter ships paying private tolls is unseemly.
reasons.hsd: Pad power and schedules leave our control.

answers.text: Keep the pads under the Directorate, at cost
answers.sub: Landings are scheduled for safety, not by price.

reasons.hsd: Landing slots stay tied to power and safety reserves.
reasons.upa: Our convoys land on engineering terms, not tolls.
reasons.lme: Another income stream locked up by engineers.
reasons.hac: Our cargo waits on a Directorate schedule.

answers.text: Free pads for local craft, fees on Earth ships
answers.sub: Local landers fly free. Earth shippers pay the treasury.

reasons.fam: Arcadian ground, Arcadian rules at the gate.
reasons.cas: The colony sets its own duties at last.
reasons.mca: Taxing Charter ships is a customs border with Earth.
reasons.hac: Our ships pay for separatist symbolism.
reasons.lme: Local trade flies free, and local merchants gain.

situations.title: Close the Airlock
situations.question: Will you sign the warrant to arrest Valdivia for sedition?
situations.body: Ezra Valdivia, 27, founded Free Arcadia. On the pirate Dustline he told the tube to 'close the airlock on Geneva'. The broadcast reached every Free Arcadia block. The Constabulary wants a sedition warrant under Charter Article 19.

answers.text: Sign the Article 19 sedition warrant
answers.sub: Valdivia is detained tonight and held for trial.
answers.gripWhy: The movement's founder jailed for a broadcast.

reasons.aco: Sedition met with Charter law. Our authority stands.
reasons.mca: Secession talk is answered before it spreads.
reasons.fam: Jailing our founder for words is a declaration of war.
reasons.cas: Arresting a speaker chills every debate in our chamber.
reasons.riw: Today Valdivia, tomorrow our union stewards.

answers.text: Refuse: it was speech, not sedition
answers.sub: No warrant. Valdivia keeps broadcasting.
answers.gripWhy: Separatist speech goes unpunished.

reasons.fam: The governor admits Arcadians may speak of freedom.
reasons.cas: Free speech protects every bench in our chamber.
reasons.aco: A soft governor lets the armed Pressure Cells grow.
reasons.mca: Geneva sees a governor shielding a secessionist.

answers.text: Cut his signal off the relays, no arrest
answers.sub: The Directorate cuts his signal, citing relay overload.
answers.gripWhy: A broadcast silenced by engineering order.

reasons.hsd: Relay capacity is a systems matter, rightly ours.
reasons.aco: The signal is down without making a martyr.
reasons.fam: Censorship dressed up as a technical report.
reasons.cas: Engineers deciding who may broadcast is dangerous.
reasons.mca: Sedition goes unpunished behind a technicality.

situations.title: Deck 4 Council
situations.question: Will you let the crews' own council run Greenhouse Deck 4?
situations.body: Greenhouse crews ask to run Deck 4 as a cooperative. An elected union council would set planting and shares. The deck would leave the Directorate's food plan.

answers.text: Give Deck 4 to an elected union council
answers.sub: Crews plant and share by council vote.

reasons.riw: The first deck held in common by its workers.
reasons.fam: Arcadian hands feeding Arcadians, no Geneva in between.
reasons.hsd: A hole in our food plan before storm season.
reasons.lme: Today one deck goes to councils, tomorrow ours.

answers.text: Keep Deck 4 under the food plan
answers.sub: The Directorate sets planting. Crews work to schedule.

reasons.hsd: One food plan, one set of reserves.
reasons.hac: Union councils stay away from colony assets.
reasons.riw: The decks stay the engineers', the work stays ours.
reasons.fam: The Directorate still rations what Arcadians grow.

situations.title: Retire Dome 3
situations.question: Dome 3 leaks air every day. Will you empty it?
situations.body: Dome 3 loses 0.4 percent of its air each day. The Directorate wants to close it and move its 2,100 residents into the lava tube. Dome 3's members in the Assembly refuse to vote for it.

answers.text: Close Dome 3 and move 2,100 into the tube
answers.sub: Dome 3 is sealed off. Residents move within 30 days.

reasons.hsd: The worst leak in the colony stops for good.
reasons.fam: Two thousand more settlers under Arcadian rock.
reasons.cas: Our members' voters uprooted by engineers' order.
reasons.aco: Two thousand angry movers crowd the tube.

answers.text: Pay Exchange contractors to reseal Dome 3
answers.sub: Private crews reseal Dome 3 on a paid contract.

reasons.lme: A public contract paid to our fabrication shops.
reasons.hac: Our sealant stock sells at full price.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified crews patching a dome we condemned.
reasons.riw: Repair work handed to private crews.
reasons.cas: Dome 3's residents keep their homes.

answers.text: Ask Geneva for a Dome 3 sealant grant
answers.sub: Earth pays for sealant. Repairs wait for the next ships.

reasons.mca: The colony turns to Geneva for rescue, as intended.
reasons.cas: Residents stay put and our chamber is heard.
reasons.hsd: The leak goes on for months awaiting Earth cargo.
reasons.aco: Charter channels, Charter order.

situations.title: Earth's Auditors Arrive
situations.question: Earth's auditors want every account and raw reserve figure. Will you open them?
situations.body: Auditors from the Charter Authority, Earth's colonial office in Geneva, have arrived. They want the Assembly's tax accounts. They also want the Directorate's raw air-reserve data. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran and Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist both call it spying for Geneva.

answers.text: Open both sets of books to the auditors
answers.sub: They see the tax books and raw reserve logs.

reasons.mca: We pay for this colony. We should see its books.
reasons.aco: Earth oversight keeps everyone honest.
reasons.cas: Earth clerks reading our tax votes line by line.
reasons.hsd: Outsiders who are not engineers questioning our raw data.
reasons.fam: Proof the colony still belongs to Geneva.

answers.text: Close the books: Arcadia audits itself
answers.sub: Auditors get summaries. Local auditors keep the full accounts.

reasons.cas: The tax belongs to the chamber that votes it.
reasons.fam: At last, a governor shuts the door on Geneva.
reasons.hsd: Our reserve data stays with those who certify it.
reasons.mca: Refusing a Charter audit defies the Charter itself.
reasons.hac: Our lenders lose a clean Earth audit of the colony.

situations.title: Storm Rationing Powers
situations.question: The storm cuts the air forecast to 150 days. Will you override the Assembly?
situations.body: A dust storm is coming. The oxygen forecast falls to 150 days, below the Charter's 180-day minimum. The Directorate, the engineers who run the plants, wants power to ration air, overruling the Assembly, while the storm lasts. The three-tone chime opened the reserve reading.

answers.text: Give the Directorate rationing powers over the Assembly
answers.sub: Engineers set air and power rations by order.
answers.gripWhy: Rationing by order, bypassing the elected Assembly.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, not a vote in the chamber.
reasons.mca: A firm hand through the storm.
reasons.cas: Engineers suspend our vote on rations.
reasons.riw: Rations cut from above. Our shift crews are hit first.
reasons.lme: Power cuts will hit private shops first.

answers.text: Let elected block and shift councils share rations
answers.sub: Elected councils split each dome's air and power share.
answers.gripWhy: Rationing handed to elected councils.

reasons.riw: The people who make the air share it out.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks finally run their own air.
reasons.hsd: Fifty councils guessing at reserves in a storm.
reasons.aco: No clear chain of command through the storm.
reasons.lme: The councils will ration the arcade before their blocks.

answers.text: Sell spare air through tradeable credits
answers.sub: Basic rations stay. Extra air is bought and sold.

reasons.lme: Air credits become a legal market, and ours to run.
reasons.hac: Scarce air gets a proper price, as it should.
reasons.riw: Crews who make the air must buy it back.
reasons.fam: Earth money buys Arcadian breath.
reasons.hsd: Prices are no substitute for a reserve plan.

situations.title: Shelters for a Tax Break
situations.question: The Exchange will build three shelters. Will you waive its tax for two years?
situations.body: The Merchants' Exchange offers to pay for three storm shelters in the Erebus Tube, the lava tube where the Mars-born districts are. In return, its members want two years free of the colony tax. The treasury would lose that income.

answers.text: Take the shelters and grant the tax break
answers.sub: Three shelters open. Exchange trade pays no tax.

reasons.lme: Two tax-free years for three shelters is a bargain.
reasons.hac: A governor who rewards private investment.
reasons.cas: The tax is ours to vote, not yours to waive.
reasons.riw: Merchants pay nothing while crews pay full tax.
reasons.fam: Shelters in the tube, whoever pays for them.

answers.text: Raise a tax and let union crews build
answers.sub: Union maintenance gangs build the shelters on public pay.

reasons.riw: Paid shelter work for union gangs.
reasons.fam: The tube built by its own people.
reasons.lme: A new tax to pay the union's wages.
reasons.cas: A tax raised without a full debate in the chamber.

situations.title: Concourse for Pressure Day
situations.question: Governor, will you open your concourse to the Pressure Day rally?
situations.body: Valdivia, Free Arcadia's leader, sits in a Dome 1 cell for sedition. His movement wants the Erebus concourse, the tube's main hall, for one sol, a Mars day. Major Novak-Sato says 6,000 people would block three emergency airlocks. 'Air Is Ours' is already painted on the gates.

answers.text: Grant the concourse for a full sol
answers.sub: Movement marshals run it. Police watch from the airlocks.

reasons.fam: The tube sees the Mars-born can gather openly.
reasons.cas: Our self-government members ride the crowd's energy.
reasons.riw: Our young members march with their neighbours.
reasons.aco: Six thousand people at three airlocks, and we stand aside.
reasons.mca: Geneva's own governor licenses a sedition suspect's rally.

answers.gripWhy: A banned movement gets the colony's biggest hall.

answers.text: Ban the rally under airlock safety rules
answers.sub: Concourse sealed. Police hold the gates all sol.

reasons.aco: The airlocks stay ours and the crowd stays home.
reasons.mca: Charter safety law applied without blinking.
reasons.hsd: No crowd crushing the emergency airlocks.
reasons.fam: Valdivia jailed, and now his people locked out too.
reasons.cas: Our voters banned from their own concourse.

answers.gripWhy: The concourse is sealed by police order.

answers.text: Move it to the Ice Field 7 hall
answers.sub: Union stewards host. It becomes a joint meeting.

reasons.riw: Our hall, our stewards, our voice in the movement.
reasons.aco: Out of the concourse, away from the main airlocks.
reasons.fam: The union steals our day and our crowd.
reasons.hsd: Politics packed beside the oxygen plant's feed lines.
reasons.hac: A strike hall turned into a protest hall.

situations.title: Passage for the Frail
situations.question: Will you pay passage home for 300 frail settlers, Governor?
situations.body: Dr. Begić, the chief medical officer, lists 300 settlers over 70 or with failing lungs. The Charter would pay their berths home on the fleet's return trip. Each one who leaves eases the air supply. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran's members call it a cull dressed up as medicine.

answers.text: Accept Charter-paid passage, strictly voluntary
answers.sub: Geneva pays the berths. Doctors confirm each person's consent.

reasons.mca: Our rescue promise to Earth citizens, seen working.
reasons.hsd: Three hundred fewer people drawing on thin oxygen reserves.
reasons.aco: Families with Earth pensions see Geneva keep its word.
reasons.cas: Our elderly shipped off the roll before the vote.
reasons.fam: Geneva thins the roll and calls it care.

answers.text: Refuse: Arcadia cares for its own elderly
answers.sub: No berths home. The colony looks after its frail.

reasons.fam: Arcadians do not send their elders away.
reasons.cas: The roll stays whole, and the chamber is heard.
reasons.mca: Refusing Charter rescue sets a dangerous precedent.
reasons.hsd: Three hundred more on reserves near the minimum.

answers.text: Let families buy berths through the Exchange
answers.sub: Seats sold at cost. The Exchange arranges the sales.

reasons.lme: Broker fees, and a new market in passage.
reasons.hac: Return berths sell through our cargo slots.
reasons.riw: Only the rich get a ticket home.
reasons.cas: Pricing rescue like cargo insults every member.
reasons.mca: Charter rescue is a right, not something sold.

situations.title: A Seat for Full Shifts
situations.question: Will you seat the union on the allocation board for full shifts?
situations.body: The 72-hour strike ended, but the slowdown did not. Ice deliveries run 20 percent short. Kamau-Quispe, head of the Ice Workers' Union, wants one permanent vote on the board that shares out power, air and water. Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist says votes do not belong beside gauges.

answers.text: Give the union a permanent board seat
answers.sub: One union vote on every power, air and water decision.

reasons.riw: The people who mine the ice now share it out.
reasons.fam: Tube workers get a hand on the air.
reasons.hsd: A union vote over certified reserve figures.
reasons.hac: Our quotas now answer to the crews.
reasons.lme: Union hands on the power we buy.

answers.gripWhy: Elected union voice enters the allocation board.

answers.text: Keep the board to certified engineers only
answers.sub: The union may read the figures, but gets no vote.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, not the picket line.
reasons.hac: Quotas stay with managers and engineers.
reasons.upa: An engineers' board is one Utopia can trust.
reasons.riw: The slowdown goes on until the board opens.
reasons.cas: Once again, no elected voice on the board.

answers.text: Pay a delivery bonus to end the slowdown
answers.sub: Treasury and Helion-Ares pay a bonus per tonne.

reasons.riw: Money in hand, though the board stays shut.
reasons.hac: Tonnage back without giving up control.
reasons.lme: Ice flows and trade runs again.
reasons.hsd: Buying shifts leaves the next strike unsolved.
reasons.cas: Tax money spent without our vote.

situations.title: Asking for Marines
situations.question: Will you formally ask Geneva for a battalion of Charter Marines?
situations.body: Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau's message is short. Ask, and 400 Charter Marines, Earth's soldiers, sail with the Window Fleet from Earth. Refuse, and Geneva will remember. The Constabulary, the colony's police, has 600 officers. Dustline, the pirate radio, already calls any request an invasion order.

answers.text: Sign the request for 400 Marines
answers.sub: A battalion sails with the fleet under Charter command.

reasons.mca: The governor invites Charter troops. Secession has its answer.
reasons.hac: Marines protect our bonds and plants alike.
reasons.aco: Marines could take our posts and our budget.
reasons.fam: The governor sent for Earth's guns.
reasons.upa: A Marine battalion a few thousand km east.
reasons.cas: Troops requested without a word to the chamber.

answers.gripWhy: Earth troops invited to back your rule.

answers.text: Decline: Arcadia keeps its own peace
answers.sub: No request sent. Security stays in local hands.

reasons.fam: No soldiers sent for against the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: The chamber's warning was heeded.
reasons.aco: No Marine officers over our heads.
reasons.mca: Refusing Charter protection smells of separatism.
reasons.hac: Our plants stay guarded by just 600 police.

answers.text: Ask for engineers and spares instead
answers.sub: Fleet berths go to reactor crews and oxygen-plant parts.

reasons.hsd: Berths for parts and crews, not rifles.
reasons.upa: No Marines pointed west.
reasons.mca: We offered security, and the governor haggles.
reasons.aco: Reinforcements refused while the tube simmers.
reasons.riw: Earth crews in the halls undercut union shifts.

situations.title: Dark Shops, Live Air
situations.question: Will you shut the Exchange's workshops to power the air plants?
situations.body: The storm has cut solar output to 60 percent. The merchants' fabrication shops by the Pad Field use 9 percent of colony power. The Directorate wants them shut until the dust clears. Chair Castellanos-Abe says 400 contracts die with them.

answers.text: Shut the shops; send power to air plants
answers.sub: Workshops dark for the storm. Their power makes oxygen.

reasons.hsd: Every spare kilowatt holds up the oxygen reserve.
reasons.riw: Oxygen-plant crews get steady power.
reasons.mca: Air before commerce, as the Charter demands.
reasons.lme: Four hundred contracts killed by decree.
reasons.hac: Our workshop orders stall for 51 sols.

answers.gripWhy: Private shops closed by Directorate order.

answers.text: Keep shops open; Exchange buys its own cells
answers.sub: Shops run on imported power cells, paid by owners.

reasons.lme: Trade survives the storm on our own money.
reasons.hac: Cell sales and workshop orders both continue.
reasons.cas: Our members' businesses spared a shutdown.
reasons.hsd: Power risk left in merchants' hands.
reasons.riw: Shops hum while plant shifts get cut.

answers.text: Shops run at night under union power limits
answers.sub: Shift councils ration shop power hour by hour.

reasons.riw: Workers decide who draws power and when.
reasons.fam: Councils over Exchange owners suits the tube.
reasons.lme: Union clerks rationing our machines.
reasons.hsd: Councils guessing at power loads.
reasons.hac: Our contractors bow to shift councils.

situations.title: Cells at Any Price
situations.question: Whose power cells will you buy to ride out the storm?
situations.body: Helion-Ares, the Earth company holding the colony's debt, offers 80 emergency power cells at triple the contract price, paid now. Director Wen of Utopia Planitia, the rival settlement, offers cheaper cells by rover. Twelve Utopian technicians come to install them. The treasury already loses ₵150M a month.

answers.text: Pay Helion-Ares the triple price
answers.sub: Cells arrive on contract. Helion-Ares keeps its monopoly.

reasons.hac: Storm profits at triple price, contract intact.
reasons.lme: Earth supply lines stay open for trade.
reasons.upa: Our offer spurned for the monopoly.
reasons.riw: Ice money poured into company profit.
reasons.cas: Tax money drained without debate.

answers.text: Take Utopia's cells and technicians
answers.sub: Twelve Utopian engineers work inside the colony's control room.

reasons.upa: Our people inside Arcadia's plants at last.
reasons.hsd: Cheaper cells, skilled hands, reserves saved.
reasons.hac: Our supply monopoly broken mid-storm.
reasons.mca: Utopian crews inside a Charter colony's plants.
reasons.aco: Foreign technicians behind our airlock codes.

answers.text: Build cells in the tube workshops
answers.sub: Mars-born makers build from salvage. Slower, but ours.

reasons.fam: Arcadian hands keep Arcadian lights on.
reasons.lme: Tube shops win the salvage contracts.
reasons.hsd: Untested cells on certified circuits.
reasons.hac: The colony learns to do without us.
reasons.upa: Arcadia leans on neither neighbour.

situations.title: The Debt's Second Price
situations.question: Will you give Helion-Ares a board seat to delay the debt?
situations.body: A ₵1.2 billion debt payment is due and needs delaying. Helion-Ares now wants more than ice rights. It wants a vote on the Directorate's board and a limit on the Assembly's power to tax. Dust still covers the solar fields. The Speaker calls it a mortgage on the chamber.

answers.text: Grant the board seat and the tax limit
answers.sub: Debt delayed. Helion-Ares votes on reserves. Taxes capped.

reasons.hac: Our money now gets a vote on the reserves.
reasons.lme: Capped taxes mean lighter taxes on trade.
reasons.cas: The tax is our one real power.
reasons.hsd: A lender voting on air allocation.
reasons.riw: The company now votes on our quotas.

answers.text: Refuse; put the plant under worker audit
answers.sub: Union auditors open the company's ice-plant books.

reasons.riw: The books that set our quotas, opened.
reasons.fam: Earth money told no in the tube's name.
reasons.hac: Union auditors in our plant: a red line.
reasons.lme: Credit dries up when lenders are audited.
reasons.mca: A Charter colony provoking its lenders.

answers.text: Ask Geneva to guarantee the delay
answers.sub: The Charter Authority backs the debt and sets the terms.

reasons.mca: The colony's debt runs through Geneva again.
reasons.aco: The Charter chain of command holds firm.
reasons.hac: Geneva's terms are softer than ours.
reasons.cas: Our finances handed back to Earth.
reasons.fam: Another Earth leash on Arcadian ice.

situations.title: Reactor Two Runs Hot
situations.question: Will you take Reactor Two down now, or run it hot?
situations.body: Reactor Two's cooling loop runs 14 degrees over its limit. Repairs need 30 sols offline. Utopian crews could cut that to 20. Running it keeps the lights on through the storm, until it shuts itself down in an emergency.

answers.text: Take it down; repair with Utopian crews
answers.sub: Power rationed during repair. Utopian crews inside the reactor.

reasons.hsd: A planned shutdown beats an emergency one.
reasons.upa: Our engineers inside Arcadia's reactor.
reasons.lme: Rationed power during the storm guts trade.
reasons.hac: Utopians working on a reactor we built.
reasons.mca: Utopian hands on a Charter reactor.

answers.gripWhy: Power rationed by order during the repair.

answers.text: Run it hot; keep the shops powered
answers.sub: Full power to the domes. Repairs after the storm.

reasons.lme: Shops and arcade stay lit through the dust.
reasons.hac: No Utopian crews, and contracts keep running.
reasons.hsd: Betting the colony's power on a failing loop.
reasons.riw: Our operators stand beside an overheating reactor.
reasons.upa: Our help refused for a dangerous bet.

situations.title: The Tube Watches
situations.question: Will you let the Tube Watches patrol your lava tube?
situations.body: Two hundred Mars-born under 25 wear rust-red armbands and walk the tube at night. They want legal standing to replace police posts. Commandant Osei-Brandt calls them Free Arcadia's militia. Graffiti of the Pressure Cells, the movement's violent fringe, appears near their meeting point.

answers.text: Deputise the Watches for the tube districts
answers.sub: Armbands become legal. Police leave the inner tube.

reasons.fam: Arcadians policing Arcadia: the first step to self-rule.
reasons.cas: Local policing by local faces.
reasons.aco: A Free Arcadia militia given our posts.
reasons.mca: A separatist force with a Charter warrant.
reasons.lme: Who protects arcade stock from armbands?

answers.gripWhy: Policing handed to the tube's own youth.

answers.text: Disband them; the police hold the tube
answers.sub: Armbands banned. Major Novak-Sato doubles the patrols.

reasons.aco: One armed service in the tube: ours.
reasons.mca: No militia under the Charter.
reasons.fam: Youth banned and patrolled will join the Cells.
reasons.cas: Doubled patrols in our members' districts.
reasons.riw: More police near the halls and picket lines.

answers.gripWhy: Armbands banned and patrols doubled.

answers.text: Fold them into union block wardens
answers.sub: Union wardens train them. No weapons, set shift rosters.

reasons.riw: Youth on union rosters, not militia lists.
reasons.hsd: Trained wardens watching airlocks and leaks.
reasons.fam: Our Watches swallowed by the union.
reasons.aco: Union wardens doing police work.
reasons.hac: The union grows a street arm.

situations.title: Inquiry Into Train 3
situations.question: Governor, will you let union investigators into Train 3?
situations.body: Sabatier Train 3, a plant that recovers water and methane, burned at shift change. Two operators are dead. Water and methane recovery is down 30 percent. The Directorate has sealed the hall for a closed review. Ice Field 7 crews wear black tape on their gloves.

answers.text: Order a public inquiry with union investigators
answers.sub: Union investigators read the logs. Hearings are broadcast.

reasons.riw: Our own people finally read the logs that killed ours.
reasons.hsd: Untrained union eyes in a sealed plant, doubting our checks.
reasons.hac: Public hearings put our quota pressure on the record.
reasons.cas: Open hearings give the Assembly a seat at the table.
reasons.aco: Union investigators in a sealed hall weaken airlock discipline.

answers.gripWhy: A public inquiry opens Directorate records to everyone.

answers.text: Keep the closed Directorate review
answers.sub: Certified engineers only. Findings released once the plant is safe.

reasons.riw: Two of ours dead, and the bosses grade their own work.
reasons.hsd: Engineers judge engineering. The plant stays ours to fix.
reasons.hac: A closed review keeps quotas out of the findings.
reasons.fam: Geneva's engineers bury Mars-born dead behind sealed doors.
reasons.upa: A disciplined technical bureau is the partner we prefer.

answers.gripWhy: The findings stay sealed inside the control room.

answers.text: Give it to a Charter inspector from Earth
answers.sub: Earth safety law applies. Findings go to Geneva first.

reasons.mca: Charter law reaches the plants, as the Charter intends.
reasons.hsd: Earth clerks twenty minutes away grading our plants.
reasons.aco: Earth law, and a clear chain up to Geneva.
reasons.riw: Geneva's inspector answers to Geneva, not to the crews.
reasons.cas: The Assembly is cut out again, in favour of Earth.

situations.title: Who Judges Valdivia
situations.question: Governor, who will you let judge Ezra Valdivia?
situations.body: Valdivia's trial opens next sol. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran wants twelve settlers as jurors. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau wants a Charter judge sitting from Earth by video link, with a twenty-minute signal delay. The tube has chalked the trial date on every airlock.

answers.text: Seat a jury of twelve settlers
answers.sub: Arcadians judge an Arcadian. Geneva watches on the link.

reasons.fam: Ezra faces his own people, not a screen from Earth.
reasons.cas: The Assembly wins: settlers sit in judgement.
reasons.mca: A colonial jury for sedition sets a secession precedent.
reasons.aco: Tube jurors will free the man who called for this.
reasons.upa: Every crack in Geneva's rule helps the west.

answers.gripWhy: Justice moves from Charter judges to settler jurors.

answers.text: Let the Charter judge sit alone
answers.sub: Sedition breaks Charter law, so Geneva's judge decides.

reasons.mca: Charter crimes are judged by the Charter. No exceptions.
reasons.aco: Our arrest stands before a judge who will convict.
reasons.fam: An Earth screen sentencing a Mars-born. That is occupation.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's call for a jury is simply ignored.
reasons.lme: A show trial means riots, and riots close the arcade.

answers.gripWhy: Geneva's judge overrides the settlers' claim to judge.

answers.text: Hire a neutral bench of Earth arbitrators
answers.sub: Exchange-paid lawyers. Costly, but neither Geneva's nor the tube's.

reasons.lme: Paid judges keep things calm, and calm sells.
reasons.hac: Hired arbiters set a precedent our contracts welcome.
reasons.mca: Sedition farmed out to hired lawyers. Charter justice sold.
reasons.fam: Bought judges are still Earth's judges.
reasons.cas: The Assembly asked for settlers and got contractors.

situations.title: The Price of Spares
situations.question: Governor, what will you give Utopia for these spares?
situations.body: Fourteen Utopian rovers stand at the Pad Field gates. They hauled 40 tonnes of oxygen-plant spares 3,800 km overland. Director Wen wants a lease on Ice Field 9 and a Utopian crew in the Control Ring, the colony's control room. Helion-Ares says Field 9 is its export claim.

answers.text: Seat a Utopian crew under Directorate checks
answers.sub: Utopian technicians work the plant. Haddad-Lindqvist signs off their work.

reasons.upa: Our engineers inside the Ring. That is our foothold.
reasons.hsd: Skilled hands on the plant, certified to our standard.
reasons.hac: Utopian crews beside our plant, eyeing our ice.
reasons.mca: A rival state inside the Charter's life-support bureau.
reasons.aco: Foreign technicians behind locks we cannot inspect.

answers.text: Pay for the spares in credits, no lease
answers.sub: Buy the 40 tonnes outright. Field 9 stays Helion-Ares's claim.

reasons.hac: Our export claim honoured. Business stays business.
reasons.lme: A cash deal, no strings. That is how trade should run.
reasons.upa: Credits are not influence. We wanted a foothold.
reasons.hsd: Spares on the plant, whoever pays for them.

answers.text: Lease Field 9 to Utopia, without Geneva
answers.sub: A deal between colonies, signed here, not in Geneva.

reasons.upa: Arcadia signs with its neighbour directly. Geneva is bypassed.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice, leased by Arcadians, to whom we choose.
reasons.mca: A treaty without the Charter. That is secession.
reasons.hac: Our export claim handed to a rival state.
reasons.aco: Utopian crews on an ice field we must now police.

situations.title: Jamming Dustline
situations.question: Governor, will you sign the order to jam Dustline?
situations.body: Dustline, a pirate radio, reaches every Free Arcadia block from a mobile transmitter. Mira Solheim reads Valdivia's letters on air every night. Commandant Osei-Brandt wants to tap the Habitat Channel, the colony's public network, and jam the tube relays.

answers.text: Approve monitoring and jam Dustline
answers.sub: Police tap the Channel. Jammers go on every tube relay.

reasons.aco: Sedition off the air, and our officers can finally listen.
reasons.mca: Seditious broadcasts silenced under Charter emergency law.
reasons.fam: They want to silence the voice of the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: Taps on the Channel will reach our own sittings.
reasons.lme: Jammers on the relays scramble arcade traffic too.

answers.gripWhy: Police watch the colony's one public channel.

answers.text: Refuse; Dustline stays on the air
answers.sub: No taps, no jammers. Nobody watches the Channel.

reasons.fam: Mira keeps reading. The tube keeps listening.
reasons.cas: No one taps the Channel the Assembly speaks on.
reasons.aco: Rebels broadcast freely while we patrol blind.
reasons.mca: The governor shelters a separatist transmitter.
reasons.upa: Loud Areanists keep Geneva busy. Good for the west.

answers.gripWhy: The pirate channel is allowed on the colony's air.

situations.title: Money of Our Own
situations.question: Governor, will you let your colony print its own money?
situations.body: Charter credits, Earth's money, run short every month. The Exchange proposes sol scrip: local notes you can trade for ice from its stocks. Geneva's money office calls it leaving Earth by the back door. Arcade boards already show a scrip price.

answers.text: Let the Exchange issue scrip backed by ice
answers.sub: The Exchange prints scrip; the treasury accepts it for taxes.

reasons.lme: We print the money. The arcade becomes the colony's bank.
reasons.fam: Arcadian money. One more thing Geneva no longer holds.
reasons.cas: Local money the Assembly can tax and vote on.
reasons.mca: The governor herself licenses a break from Earth's money.
reasons.hac: Our bonds are in credits. Scrip leads to default.

answers.text: Pay workers tokens for air and food
answers.sub: Union-run tokens, paid for each shift worked.

reasons.riw: Air earned by the hands that mine the ice.
reasons.fam: Mars-made money, owned by the workers.
reasons.lme: Labour tokens cut us out of our own trade.
reasons.hac: Worker money and ice: first step to seizing our plant.
reasons.hsd: Tokens undercut the ration we certify.

answers.text: Issue Directorate power credits instead
answers.sub: Notes backed by power, counted in the engineers' control room.

reasons.hsd: Money tied to measured reserves cannot be inflated.
reasons.upa: Money run by engineers. Utopia runs on the same idea.
reasons.lme: The engineers hold the money; we lose our bank.
reasons.mca: Any colony money breaks from Earth, metered or not.
