reasons.riw: Engineers metering our wages in kilowatts. No.

situations.title: Below the Safe Line
situations.question: Governor, oxygen is below the safe line. What will you tell Geneva?
situations.body: The reserve report puts oxygen at 141 days. The Charter's legal minimum is 180. Article 31 lets you declare a Margin Emergency, handing air and power to the engineers. The Directorate offers to recount, counting spares not yet arrived. Helion-Ares bondholders read every report.

answers.text: Report the shortfall to the Charter Authority today
answers.sub: The 141-day figure goes to Geneva, checked and unchanged.

reasons.mca: The shortfall is reported, as the Charter requires.
reasons.aco: The chain to Geneva holds, by the book.
reasons.hsd: Our checked figure goes out unaltered.
reasons.hac: A reported shortfall sends our bond price down.
reasons.lme: Earth traders will treat the colony as failing.

answers.text: Declare a Margin Emergency under Article 31
answers.sub: Engineers share out power and air; the Assembly loses its votes.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide now, as they always should have.
reasons.upa: Engineers in charge. A governor Utopia understands.
reasons.cas: Our say over reserves taken by decree.
reasons.lme: Emergency sharing means our stock gets seized.
reasons.riw: Engineers rule the halls, and crews get no say.

answers.gripWhy: Emergency powers take air and power from elected hands.

answers.text: Quietly recount to calm the bondholders
answers.sub: Spares counted early; the shortfall stays off the report.

reasons.hac: No shortfall on paper, no run on our bonds.
reasons.lme: The arcade trades another quarter without panic.
reasons.mca: A hidden breach of the Charter minimum. Grounds for recall.
reasons.hsd: Counting spares not installed is faking the reserve.
reasons.riw: Our crews breathe the real figure, not the paper one.

answers.gripWhy: The true reserve is hidden from Geneva and the street.

situations.title: The Charter Oath
situations.question: Governor, will you make the Mars-born swear Geneva's oath?
situations.body: The settler roll counts 11,400 Mars-born. Geneva's new order: Earth citizenship only after a loyalty oath to the Charter, sworn before a roll clerk. Free Arcadia has called for burning roll cards in the Erebus Tube, the main hall of the colony's lava tube.

answers.text: Give the oath; no oath, no Earth passport
answers.sub: Clerks swear in every Mars-born; refusers lose Earth citizenship.

reasons.mca: Every Mars-born bound to the Charter by oath.
reasons.aco: Sworn citizens, and a clear list of who refused.
reasons.fam: The oath is our red line. The cards will burn.
reasons.cas: Citizenship by loyalty test, forced without a vote.
reasons.riw: Our young crews forced to swear to Geneva.

answers.gripWhy: Citizenship tied to a loyalty oath, checked by clerks.

answers.text: Refuse the oath; register Mars-born as Arcadians
answers.sub: The roll lists them as Arcadian-born, with no Earth oath.

reasons.fam: Arcadians on paper at last. No leash, no oath.
reasons.cas: The self-government bloc wins its first written recognition.
reasons.mca: A governor who refuses the Charter's own roll.
reasons.aco: We cannot police a roll Geneva does not recognise.
reasons.upa: A separate people means a separate partner for us.

answers.gripWhy: Citizenship stops being a loyalty test.

situations.title: Common Kitchens
situations.question: Governor, will you feed the tube from shared kitchens?
situations.body: Food is short; the storm has dimmed the greenhouse decks. The RIWU, the ice workers' union, wants shared kitchens in every tube block, staffed by its crews. Utopia Planitia offers two tonnes of algae protein a month. Exchange food stalls would lose their trade.

answers.text: Open union kitchens with Utopian algae
answers.sub: Union crews cook; Utopian protein fills the pots.

reasons.riw: Food in common, shared by those who earn it.
reasons.upa: Utopian protein on every tube table. Influence by the bowl.
reasons.fam: The tube eats together, and not from Geneva.
reasons.lme: Free kitchens close every food stall in the arcade.
reasons.mca: Arcadians fed by Utopia. A dependence we forbid.

answers.text: Pay Exchange stalls to sell cheap meals
answers.sub: The treasury pays the stalls; private cooks feed the blocks.

reasons.lme: Paid contracts for every stall in the tube.
reasons.hac: Private supply, not union councils. Sound policy.
reasons.riw: Profit off hungry crews, on the treasury's bill.
reasons.upa: Our algae refused so the arcade can profit.
reasons.fam: Merchants selling the Mars-born their own rations back.

situations.title: The Arcadian Congress
situations.question: Governor, will you give their Congress a voice in your decrees?
situations.body: Three hundred block delegates met in the basalt gallery under Free Arcadia's two-moon banner. They call it the Arcadian Congress. They want to read every decree before you sign it. Geneva calls it a rival government.

answers.text: Recognise the Congress as an advisory body
answers.sub: Every decree goes to the Congress to read first.

reasons.fam: Our people now have a chamber the governor listens to.
reasons.upa: A second authority in the tube. We can talk to it.
reasons.mca: Recognising an authority beside the Charter. Our red line.
reasons.cas: A rival chamber in the tube outflanks the elected Assembly.
reasons.aco: The governor blesses a body that shelters the militant Pressure Cells.

answers.gripWhy: A street body gains a formal say over decrees.

answers.text: Fold its delegates into union block councils
answers.sub: Delegates sit on union councils that share out supplies.

reasons.riw: Block councils grow, and sharing moves toward the crews.
reasons.cas: No rival chamber. The Assembly stays the only one.
reasons.fam: Our Congress dissolved into union committees.
reasons.hsd: Block councils meddling in supply. Reserves by show of hands.
reasons.mca: Union councils are still councils outside the Charter.

situations.title: The Tankers Stand Idle
situations.question: Governor, will you write the union's say into law to end this?
situations.body: The ice tankers at Ice Field 7 have stood idle for nine sols, or Mars days. The water reserve is 231 days and falls a day each sol. All 2,900 union members are out. Kamau-Quispe ends it only for a union seat on supply decisions, written into Assembly law.

answers.text: Send a Union Seat Bill to the Assembly
answers.sub: The union gets a legal vote on air and water.

reasons.riw: A seat in law outlasts any governor's promise.
reasons.cas: The Assembly writes the settlement and gains weight.
reasons.hsd: Union votes on reserves mean politics in the gauges.
reasons.hac: A union veto over ice threatens our export quotas.
reasons.aco: Strikers rewarded means more strikes to police.

answers.gripWhy: Power over air and water is shared with an elected union.

answers.text: Run the tankers with Directorate crews
answers.sub: Engineers drive the tankers; strikers lose their shift rations.

reasons.riw: Directorate strikebreakers in our tankers, and our rations cut.
reasons.hsd: Our trained hands restore the water line on schedule.
reasons.hac: The ice moves again and the contracts hold.
reasons.fam: Mars-born crews starved back to work.
reasons.cas: The Assembly is bypassed in a colony-wide crisis.

answers.gripWhy: Strikers are cut off and replaced by order.

answers.text: Use the Charter's essential-services clause
answers.sub: The strike becomes unlawful; police escort the tankers out.

reasons.aco: Clear Charter law puts officers behind the tankers.
reasons.mca: Charter law, not union terms, keeps the water running.
reasons.riw: Armed police at the pickets: our red line.
reasons.fam: Geneva's clause turned on Arcadian workers.
reasons.cas: A strike outlawed without the Assembly's vote.

answers.gripWhy: A strike is outlawed under emergency Charter powers.

situations.title: Who Goes Dark First
situations.question: Which domes go dark first, Governor, and will you take Utopia's cells?
situations.body: Reactor Two shut itself down in an emergency at 04:12. Domes 2 to 5 face 22 sols of low power. Oxygen sits at 141 days, below the 180-day floor. Utopia's rovers can bring fuel cells in eleven sols. Someone's lights go out first.

answers.text: Cut power by the Directorate's reserve table
answers.sub: Tube blocks go dark first; plants and hospital stay lit.

reasons.hsd: Our table, followed to the line.
reasons.aco: A fixed schedule is easier to police.
reasons.fam: The Mars-born tube goes dark again, as always.
reasons.riw: Crew homes dark while we keep the halls running.
reasons.cas: No member was asked whose district goes dark.

answers.gripWhy: The engineers decide who loses power, by order.

answers.text: Keep the tube lit, take Utopia's cells
answers.sub: Mars-born districts stay lit; Utopian rovers cross the plain.

reasons.fam: The tube lit by Martians helping Martians.
reasons.upa: Our rovers make Utopia Arcadia's true rescuer.
reasons.mca: Rescue by a rival settlement weakens the Charter's guarantee.
reasons.hac: Utopian cells undercut our supply contracts.
reasons.hsd: Untested foreign cells on our grid.

answers.text: Let the blocks bid credits for power
answers.sub: Those who pay keep their lights; the Exchange runs the auction.

reasons.lme: Our brokers run the market for scarce watts.
reasons.hac: Priced power proves the market model works.
reasons.riw: Crews can't outbid merchants for their own light.
reasons.fam: Air and light sold to the highest bidder.
reasons.cas: An auction decided outside the elected chamber.

situations.title: Slots on Nine Ships
situations.question: How will you split the fleet's cargo space, Governor?
situations.body: Loading for the Window Fleet, the supply ships from Earth, closes in Geneva in 30 days. There are nine ships, and Helion-Ares controls the cargo space. The Exchange wants room for coffee, cloth and wine at paying rates. The Directorate wants every tonne for air-plant and reactor parts.

answers.text: Sell a third of the space to Exchange cargo
answers.sub: Paying luxuries ride along; the treasury takes a fee.

reasons.lme: Real coffee in the arcade, and margins with it.
reasons.hac: Paid space covers our cargo contracts.
reasons.hsd: Every crate of wine is a missing reactor seal.
reasons.riw: Luxuries for merchants while crews breathe dust.
reasons.cas: The fee eases the tax fight.

answers.text: Every tonne goes to machinery
answers.sub: Air-plant parts, seals and reactor parts only; no luxuries.

reasons.hsd: Reserves come before every comfort.
reasons.mca: Spares on board show Geneva's rescue at work.
reasons.lme: Our paying cargo is barred from the ships.
reasons.hac: Unpaid machinery space eats our freight profits.

answers.text: Let elected crew councils vote on the space
answers.sub: Union councils list what the halls need most.

reasons.riw: The people who fix the halls choose the parts.
reasons.fam: Settlers decide, not Geneva or the Exchange.
reasons.hsd: Union lists replace our expert survey of needs.
reasons.lme: Councils will never vote space for trade.
reasons.hac: Our cargo space shared out by a union show of hands.

answers.gripWhy: Cargo decisions pass to elected crew councils.

situations.title: Flags Over the Dead
situations.question: Governor, under which flag will you let the two dead workers be mourned?
situations.body: Two operators died in the Sabatier fuel plant fire. Chaplain Oduya has booked Dome Square for a memorial under the Charter flag. Free Arcadia says one of the dead was Mars-born and wants its rust-red banner. Pirate radio Dustline calls the Charter flag an insult.

answers.text: Hold the memorial under the Charter flag
answers.sub: The Charter Hymn plays; police guard the square.

reasons.mca: The Charter honours its dead, all of them.
reasons.aco: A guarded square under one flag stays orderly.
reasons.fam: Geneva's flag over a Martian coffin.
reasons.riw: Our dead, and Earth's hymn drowns our work songs.
reasons.cas: The governor took a side at a funeral.

answers.text: Fly the Arcadian banner over the dead
answers.sub: Drums in Dome Square; the Charter flag stays furled.

reasons.fam: The two moons over Dome Square, at last.
reasons.riw: Settlers mourn our crewmates their own way.
reasons.cas: The governor listens to the settlers' mood.
reasons.mca: A secessionist banner raised in Dome 1 itself.
reasons.aco: Officers ordered to guard a Free Arcadia rally.

answers.gripWhy: A banned banner flies with your blessing.

situations.title: Kill the Bill Early?
situations.question: Will you use your Charter veto on the Self-Government Bill now?
situations.body: Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran has put the Self-Government Bill before the Assembly. The whips count 31 of 50 seats for it; 26 would pass it. A veto now kills it before any debate. Geneva is watching on the Earth link.

answers.text: Let the first debate go ahead, no veto
answers.sub: The bill is debated openly; you stay neutral on paper.

reasons.cas: The chamber does real business at last.
reasons.fam: Self-government on the floor, not in the tube.
reasons.lme: Local rule could mean local trade terms.
reasons.mca: A governor who lets secession be read aloud.
reasons.aco: We swore to a Charter you let be debated away.

answers.gripWhy: The Assembly is free to debate breaking away.

answers.text: Veto it under the Charter
answers.sub: The bill dies; the Assembly loses its main business.

reasons.mca: The Charter's veto used as Geneva intended.
reasons.aco: The chain of command up to Geneva stands.
reasons.cas: Thirty-one votes erased by one Earth clause.
reasons.fam: Proof that the Charter is a leash.

answers.gripWhy: An elected majority is silenced by veto.

answers.text: Rewrite it as a trade self-rule bill
answers.sub: Tax and tariff powers for the Assembly; no breakaway clause.

reasons.lme: Tariff powers in local hands help our trade.
reasons.hac: Trade freedom without cancelling debt suits our bonds.
reasons.cas: Real tax powers, if not the whole bill.
reasons.fam: They sold our homeland for tariff tables.
reasons.mca: Any Assembly power grab sets a precedent.

situations.title: Quarters for the Marines
situations.question: Where will you house the 400 Marines, Governor, and who commands them?
situations.body: Geneva confirms 400 Charter Marines, Earth's soldiers, aboard the Window Fleet. The Assembly wants them kept at the Pad Field, the landing ground outside the domes. Commandant Osei-Brandt wants them under his command inside Dome 1.

answers.text: Put the Marines under Osei-Brandt in Dome 1
answers.sub: One chain of command, from the police up to Geneva.

reasons.aco: The Marines reinforce us instead of replacing us.
reasons.mca: The garrison serves the Charter's lawful police.
reasons.cas: Our demand for the Pad Field was ignored.
reasons.fam: Earth soldiers inside the domes: an occupation.
reasons.upa: A Marine force in the colony's heart, aimed west.

answers.gripWhy: An armed garrison is placed inside the domes.

answers.text: Pad Field only; barred from the tube
answers.sub: Marines stay outside; settlers keep the tube's locks.

reasons.cas: Our vote decided where they sleep.
reasons.fam: Not one Earth boot below the basalt line.
reasons.upa: Marines kept at the pads point nowhere.
reasons.aco: We are left outgunned and passed over.
reasons.mca: Our battalion is fenced off like a threat.

answers.text: Assign them to guard the plants
answers.sub: Marines guard reactors and air plants under Directorate orders.

reasons.hsd: The plants are guarded from strikes and sabotage.
reasons.mca: The Marines serve, whoever directs them.
reasons.riw: Armed troops in the halls: our red line.
reasons.aco: Directorate orders, not ours, run the Marines.
reasons.upa: Marines guard the ice we want to lease.

situations.title: Ten Hours for the Hull
situations.question: Will you make every adult work ten hours a week on repairs?
situations.body: Seals are failing faster than crews can fix them. The Directorate's Systems Service would take every adult aged 16 to 60 for ten hours of repair work a week. The union calls it forced strikebreaking. Free Arcadia says Mars-born kids will scrub Earth's ducts.

answers.text: Decree the Systems Service
answers.sub: Ten hours a week, logged on service cards.

reasons.hsd: Ten thousand hands on the seal backlog.
reasons.aco: Logged service cards make a tidy register.
reasons.hac: Unpaid repairs protect our modules.
reasons.riw: Draftees doing union work for nothing.
reasons.fam: Martian youth drafted to patch Earth's hulls.
reasons.lme: Ten hours lost from every shop and stall.

answers.gripWhy: Forced labour is imposed by decree.

answers.text: Hire union crews for repairs instead
answers.sub: Union rates and rosters, paid from the treasury.

reasons.riw: Paid union work, not a labour draft.
reasons.fam: No Mars-born teenager in a duct.
reasons.hsd: Union rosters, not our schedules, set repair order.
reasons.hac: Union rates for work on our modules.

situations.title: The Council Takes the Plant
situations.question: Will you let the union take Helion-Ares's ice plant, Governor?
situations.body: Workers at the Ice Field 7 plant, which turns raw ice into water, have elected a council. They voted to run it in common. Helion-Ares built it and owns it. Its chief, Katharina Sørlie-Tan, threatens to sue in Earth courts and freeze spare parts.

answers.text: Hand the plant to the workers' council
answers.sub: Shared ownership; the union council runs the ice line.

reasons.riw: The ice belongs to those who dig it.
reasons.fam: Earth capital loses its grip on Arcadian ice.
reasons.hac: Confiscation of our plant: our red line.
reasons.lme: Today their plant, tomorrow our decks.
reasons.mca: Seizing Earth property invites Earth courts.

answers.text: Broker a share sale to Exchange investors
answers.sub: Helion-Ares sells 40 percent locally; workers get bonuses.

reasons.lme: A stake in the colony's ice at last.
reasons.hac: We sell a share on our terms and keep control.
reasons.cas: Local owners keep ice money in Arcadia.
reasons.riw: Bonuses instead of ownership: a bribe.

answers.text: Take the plant into colony ownership
answers.sub: The settlement owns Arcadia's ice, not Earth.

reasons.fam: Air Is Ours, and now the ice too.
reasons.cas: The Assembly gains a plant to govern.
reasons.riw: Better the colony than the Consortium.
reasons.hac: Seizure by a colony that owes us money.
reasons.mca: A settlement seizing property acts like a state.

situations.title: Default Day
situations.question: The loan has lapsed. Will you grant field rights, default, or seek Geneva?
situations.body: The six-month extension has run out. ₵1.2 billion is due, and the treasury cannot pay. Helion-Ares threatens default proceedings and a freeze on fleet cargo unless it gets 30-year rights to the ice fields. The Assembly is debating refusing to pay the debt at all.

answers.text: Grant 30-year field rights for an extension
answers.sub: Default avoided; Helion-Ares holds the ice fields until 2122.

reasons.hac: Thirty years of fields secures our bonds.
reasons.lme: Credit keeps flowing to the arcade.
reasons.riw: Our ice is sold for a generation.
reasons.fam: Arcadia's ice is mortgaged to Earth until 2122.
reasons.cas: The tax chamber was bypassed on the debt.

answers.text: Back refusing to pay the colonial debt
answers.sub: Arcadia calls the bonds Earth's debt, not its own.

reasons.fam: We never signed Earth's debts.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's motion carries the day.
reasons.riw: No more shifts worked to pay bondholders.
reasons.hac: Refusal to pay: all we feared from Mars-born nationalists.
reasons.mca: Refusing the debt comes one step before secession.
reasons.lme: Our Earth credit lines die with the bonds.

answers.text: Ask Geneva to guarantee the debt
answers.sub: The Charter Authority stands behind it and oversees the treasury.

reasons.mca: An Earth guarantee binds Arcadia to the Charter.
reasons.aco: Geneva's backing steadies the colony's paymaster.
reasons.hac: A Concord guarantee is better than a default.
reasons.cas: Earth auditors will now run our taxes.
reasons.fam: Geneva buys the colony's leash with its debt.

situations.title: The Cut Relay
situations.question: The relay mast is down. Will you talk, hunt or rebuild?
situations.body: Overnight the Pressure Cells, Free Arcadia's militant wing, cut the Charter relay mast on Ridge 2. Messages to Geneva now run on one backup dish. Juno Arrieta claims it on pirate radio Dustline. From detention, Ezra Valdivia sends word: he will disown the Cells publicly if you open talks.

answers.text: Open talks with Valdivia in detention
answers.sub: He disowns the Cells; you deal with Free Arcadia.

reasons.fam: Our founder at the table splits the Cells from us.
reasons.cas: Talks bring the self-government bloc into the room.
reasons.riw: Talks beat sweeps through our members' blocks.
reasons.aco: You reward the men who cut a Charter mast.
reasons.mca: Talks with a sedition suspect invite secession.

answers.gripWhy: You deal with the movement instead of policing it.

answers.text: Order the Constabulary to hunt the Pressure Cells
answers.sub: Police sweeps through the tube blocks under the sedition law.

reasons.aco: At last a clear order to take the tube back.
reasons.mca: Charter property was attacked; Charter law answers.
reasons.fam: Every Mars-born youth is a suspect in his own block.
reasons.cas: Sweeps without warrants insult the Assembly's members.
reasons.riw: Our crews live in those blocks and get searched too.

answers.gripWhy: Mass searches under the sedition law.

answers.text: Rebuild the mast under Directorate guard; no talks
answers.sub: Stronger mast, engineers on guard, no deal with anyone.

reasons.hsd: Comms are a system; we fix systems, not grievances.
reasons.upa: A governor leaning on engineers suits Utopia.
reasons.fam: Ignored again; the Cells will say only cutting works.
reasons.aco: Directorate guards do our job outside our command.
reasons.mca: Geneva wanted the culprits caught, not a better mast.

situations.title: The Ten-Year Plan
situations.question: One budget, two futures. Where will you spend your credits?
situations.body: The Directorate's ten-year plan is on your desk. Option one: drill deep for ice in the crater with rented Utopian rigs. Option two: expand the Erebus lava tube, homes under solid rock. The treasury can pay for one. Dome 3 still leaks 0.4 percent of its air a sol.

answers.text: Drill the crater with Utopian rigs
answers.sub: Deep ice for the reserves; Utopia's machines in our fields.

reasons.hsd: Deep ice is the only reserve that lasts ten years.
reasons.upa: Our rigs in Arcadia mean leases and influence.
reasons.riw: Drilling means shifts and new crews.
reasons.hac: Utopian rigs eat into our export claims.
reasons.mca: Geneva will not have Utopia drilling a Charter colony.

answers.text: Spend the budget on the lava tube
answers.sub: New basalt terraces for living under rock.

reasons.fam: The tube is Arcadian ground; build our homeland there.
reasons.cas: Members' districts get the housing they asked for.
reasons.lme: Terraces need shops and fabrication contracts.
reasons.hsd: Homes before ice is a reserve built on sand.
reasons.upa: No rigs, no lease, no foothold.

situations.title: A Seat on the Review
situations.question: Geneva trades a review seat for your public backing. Will you take it?
situations.body: In June, the Charter Review Commission begins its hearings. It reviews the Charter's future. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau offers your nominee a seat on it. The price: you publicly back renewal before the Assembly votes. The self-government bloc holds 31 of 50 seats.

answers.text: Back renewal in public and take the seat
answers.sub: Your nominee sits in Geneva. You stand with the Charter.

reasons.mca: We appointed a governor to campaign for renewal.
reasons.aco: A clear Charter line keeps our chain of command.
reasons.hac: Renewal keeps our bonds under Earth courts.
reasons.fam: The governor chose Geneva over the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: You decide our vote before we even sit.

answers.gripWhy: You side with Geneva against the elected Assembly.

answers.text: Refuse. The settlers decide on renewal.
answers.sub: No seat, no backing. The vote stays here.

reasons.fam: Geneva cannot buy Arcadia's future.
reasons.cas: Our vote stays our own.
reasons.upa: Geneva's hold weakens, and Utopia gains room.
reasons.mca: A governor neutral on the Charter is a doubtful one.
reasons.aco: We need to know whose law we enforce.

answers.text: Trade your backing for dominion terms and bond guarantees
answers.sub: Dominion means self-rule under Earth's flag, trade rights, debts secured.

reasons.lme: Dominion trade terms open Earth markets to the Exchange.
reasons.hac: Bonds written into the Charter get repaid.
reasons.cas: A revised Charter gives us the levy power we want.
reasons.mca: Geneva does not haggle over its Charter.
reasons.fam: Dominion is still a leash, only a gilded one.

situations.title: The Extradition Order
situations.question: Geneva wants Valdivia sent to Earth. Will you hand him over?
situations.body: The court cleared Ezra Valdivia of sedition. It gave him 90 sols, or Mars days, for unlawful assembly. Now the Charter Authority orders him sent to Earth on the fleet's return trip. The tube is already drumming. Mira Solheim reads the order on Dustline, the pirate channel, every hour.

answers.text: Send him to Earth on the return trip
answers.sub: He serves his 90 sols, then ships to Earth under guard.

reasons.mca: Charter law reaches every settler, Mars-born or not.
reasons.aco: Shipping him off ends the rallies at the source.
reasons.fam: Extradition is our red line. This is war on us.
reasons.cas: Overriding the court's sentence makes the trial a joke.
reasons.riw: Our tube members will walk off the job over this.

answers.gripWhy: You deport a popular leader over the court's sentence.

answers.text: Refuse. He serves his 90 sols here.
answers.sub: Sentenced in Arcadia, jailed in Arcadia, then freed.

reasons.fam: Arcadians are judged and jailed in Arcadia.
reasons.cas: The court's sentence stands as the last word.
reasons.upa: Defying Geneva shows Arcadia can stand alone.
reasons.mca: Refusing a Charter order is a step toward secession.
reasons.aco: He walks out in 90 sols and rallies again.

answers.gripWhy: You shield a dissident from Geneva.

answers.text: Release him to union custody until his appeal
answers.sub: The RIWU posts bond and guarantees he stays.

reasons.riw: Our guarantee proves the union keeps order better.
reasons.fam: Free under the workers' roof beats an Earth cell.
reasons.hsd: A union holding prisoners near the plants is a risk.
reasons.aco: Prisoners belong with officers, not a picket hall.
reasons.mca: Bail to a union does not answer a Charter order.

answers.gripWhy: A convicted man goes free into union hands.

situations.title: Water by Block
situations.question: Tube blocks now share out their own water. Will you make it law?
situations.body: Residents of 34 lava-tube blocks have elected block committees. They share out the water ration by a show of hands. The RIWU, the ice workers' union, asks you to let their counts overrule the Directorate's meters. Directorate engineers say the committees already hand out 6 percent more than planned.

answers.text: Give the block committees the final word on water
answers.sub: Elected committees share out water. Directorate meters only measure.

reasons.riw: The people who haul the ice now share the water.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks running themselves is self-government in practice.
reasons.cas: Elected bodies with real powers strengthen our case.
reasons.hsd: Sharing water by show of hands will drain the reserve.
reasons.lme: Next the committees will ration our members' private water.

answers.gripWhy: Water control passes from the plant to elected committees.

answers.text: Keep the meters under Directorate control
answers.sub: Committees may advise. The certified figure decides.

reasons.hsd: Water is a reserve to guard, not a vote.
reasons.aco: One authority over the valves means fewer fights.
reasons.hac: Engineers on the meters protect plant output.
reasons.riw: You deny the workers their own common stock.
reasons.fam: Dome 1 keeps its hand on the tube's taps.

answers.gripWhy: You overrule elected committees.

situations.title: Berths and Names
situations.question: Earth buyers want berths and names. Will you sell Arcadia's landmarks?
situations.body: The Exchange wants to sell Earth tourists berths on the next fleet. It also wants to sell naming rights to the Erebus Tube, Ice Field 7 and the Dome 1 mast. Helion-Ares would broker it for 15 percent. The treasury loses ₵1.5 every month.

answers.text: Sell the berths and names through Helion-Ares
answers.sub: Credits now. Earth logos on Arcadian landmarks.

reasons.lme: Tourists spend in the arcade, and names pay every year.
reasons.hac: Fifteen percent, and a new Earth market for us.
reasons.cas: Nobody asked us before selling public names.
reasons.fam: Branding the Erebus Tube sells our homeland by the metre.
reasons.riw: Tourists in the halls slow shifts and mock our crews.

answers.text: Refuse. No Earth brands on Arcadian rock.
answers.sub: Landmarks keep their names. The tourists stay home.

reasons.fam: Our places keep the names the Mars-born gave them.
reasons.cas: A popular stand our self-government bloc can cheer.
reasons.lme: You turn away the only new money on offer.
reasons.hac: Another Earth market closed by Areanist pride.
reasons.mca: Turning away Earth visitors sounds like closing the airlock.

situations.title: The Chief Engineer's Ultimatum
situations.question: Your chief engineer threatens to quit. Will you stop trading air for votes?
situations.body: Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist puts her resignation letter on the table in the Control Ring. The oxygen reserve is below the 180-day Charter floor. She says your office trades air reserves for Assembly votes. Her deputy waits outside, ready to run the Control Ring your way.

answers.text: Give her a binding veto on reserve trades
answers.sub: No change to air or power shares without her sign-off.

reasons.hsd: At last the gauges outrank the politics.
reasons.upa: An engineer-run Arcadia is one Utopia can deal with.
reasons.cas: We lose our say over reserves before we used it.
reasons.riw: Our allocation seat means nothing under her veto.
reasons.fam: Another Earth-trained board ruling the tube's air.

answers.gripWhy: Reserve decisions close to the Assembly and the street.

answers.text: Accept her resignation. The deputy sells reserves openly.
answers.sub: A pliant chief prices spare capacity and sells it to bidders.

reasons.lme: Priced reserves let us buy the power we need.
reasons.hac: A chief who counts costs will grant our board seat.
reasons.aco: A shaken Control Ring makes the domes nervous.
reasons.hsd: You sacked the one person who refused to cook figures.
reasons.mca: Geneva trusts her certified figures, not a deputy's.

answers.text: Put a union operator on the reserve board
answers.sub: Workers read the gauges beside the engineers.

reasons.riw: Those who run the halls should read the gauges.
reasons.fam: Mars-born operators in the Control Ring at last.
reasons.lme: Union eyes on allocation mean seizures of our stock next.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified hands on the board, just as she warned.
reasons.hac: A union on the reserve board will target our plant.

situations.title: Wen's Pact
situations.question: Director Wen offers rescue and trade. Will you sign despite Geneva's warning?
situations.body: Director Wen of Utopia Planitia, the rival settlement to the west, offers a pact. Utopia would answer any hull breach, send spares overland and buy ice. The pact recognises whatever government Arcadia ends up with. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau cables from Geneva: signing it is treason against the Charter.

answers.text: Sign the rescue and trade pact with Wen
answers.sub: Utopian rescue and spares. Geneva calls you a traitor.

reasons.upa: Arcadia leans west, and our office opens in the Domes.
reasons.lme: A second buyer for ice and a second supplier.
reasons.fam: A neighbour who will recognise us, whatever we become.
reasons.mca: A treaty with a rival power ends the Charter.
reasons.aco: We swore to the Charter, not to Utopia's pact.
reasons.hac: Utopian ice deals break our export monopoly.

answers.text: Refuse. Rescue comes only from the Charter.
answers.sub: Geneva's guarantee stands alone. Wen's convoys stop.

reasons.mca: The Charter's rescue guarantee needs no rival.
reasons.aco: One loyalty, one chain of command.
reasons.fam: You lock us onto Earth's leash again.
reasons.upa: Our offer is spurned, and the western door closes.
reasons.lme: No Utopian trade, no second buyer for our stock.

situations.title: The Dissolution Order
situations.question: Geneva orders the Assembly shut down. Will you close the chamber?
situations.body: The Self-Government Bill passed its second reading, 33 votes to 17. The Charter Authority tells you to dissolve the Colonial Assembly before the fleet arrives. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran keeps the chamber sitting through the night. Free Arcadia drummers fill the corridor outside.

answers.text: Dissolve the Assembly as Geneva instructs
answers.sub: All seats empty. The Charter rules by your decree.

reasons.mca: No chamber, no declaration, no precedent.
reasons.aco: A decree we can enforce beats a vote we cannot.
reasons.lme: Our Exchange members lose their seats with the rest.
reasons.cas: Suspending our sittings is our red line. You crossed it.
reasons.fam: Geneva shut the only voice the Mars-born had.

answers.gripWhy: You dissolve the elected chamber by decree.

answers.text: Refuse. The Assembly sits until the vote.
answers.sub: The bill runs its course. Geneva's order is shelved.

reasons.cas: The governor stands with the settlers' chamber.
reasons.fam: Now the declaration can reach the floor.
reasons.upa: Arcadia's own government takes shape, and Utopia gains.
reasons.mca: Defying a direct order is grounds for recall.
reasons.aco: We end up guarding a chamber voting for secession.

answers.gripWhy: You protect the chamber against Geneva.

answers.text: Pause it for 30 sols and broker terms
answers.sub: Sittings stop while the Exchange drafts a compromise.

reasons.lme: Thirty sols for a deal that keeps trade flowing.
reasons.hac: A pause keeps the bill away from our bonds.
reasons.mca: Half a dissolution is better than none.
reasons.cas: A pause is suspension by another name.
reasons.fam: A pause is a stall. The drums will not stop.

answers.gripWhy: You suspend the sittings to buy time.

situations.title: The Hall Is Held
situations.question: Strikers hold the electrolysis hall. Will you let them run the air?
situations.body: Day four of the nine-sol general strike. RIWU and Free Arcadia workers hold the main electrolysis hall, which splits water into oxygen. The machines still run. The strikers' council will keep the air flowing if the Constabulary stays out. Major Novak-Sato has two squads at the hall locks.

answers.text: Let the council run the hall. Police stay out.
answers.sub: Workers run the air until the strike ends.

reasons.riw: Proof the halls run without bosses or police.
reasons.fam: Workers and Mars-born holding the air together.
reasons.aco: You order officers to stand aside from an occupation.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified operators on the machines, with oxygen below the floor.
reasons.hac: Reward this occupation and our plant is next.

answers.gripWhy: You tolerate strikers seizing life support.

answers.text: Send the Constabulary to clear the hall
answers.sub: Squads go through the locks. Strike leaders are detained.

reasons.aco: Armouries and air belong under Charter command.
reasons.mca: Seizing life support is rebellion. Charter law answers it.
reasons.riw: Armed police in the halls is our red line.
reasons.fam: Constables in the hall prove Dome 1 rules by force.
reasons.cas: No vote, no warrant, just squads at the machines.

answers.gripWhy: Police storm an occupied plant.

answers.text: Directorate engineers take the controls; strikers stay
answers.sub: Engineers run the machines. The strikers keep the floor.

reasons.hsd: Certified hands on the air, whoever holds the floor.
reasons.upa: Engineers first. Utopia approves of that order.
reasons.aco: The occupation stands, and we watch from outside.
reasons.riw: You take our controls and call it neutral.
reasons.fam: The engineers serve Dome 1, as always.

answers.gripWhy: The Directorate takes the plant from the strikers.

situations.title: The League Wants Stunners
situations.question: Governor, will you arm the Charter League as Constabulary helpers?
situations.body: Four hundred Earth-born settlers signed up for the Charter League in Dome 1. They drill in the Charter Reading Room. They want stunners, lock codes and blue armbands before the fleet arrives. The Constabulary has 600 officers. Free Arcadia calls the League a settler militia.

answers.text: Swear them in as armed police helpers
answers.sub: 400 loyalists under police command, with stunners and armbands.

reasons.aco: Four hundred more loyal hands on the locks.
reasons.mca: Loyal settlers guard the Charter until the Marines land.
reasons.fam: Armed Earth-born gangs let loose on the tube.
reasons.cas: A private army that answers to Dome 1, not us.
reasons.riw: Armbands near the halls mean broken pickets.

answers.gripWhy: Armed loyalists patrol beside the police.

answers.text: Make them unarmed Directorate repair crews
answers.sub: The League drills on seals and pumps, not weapons.

reasons.hsd: Four hundred spare hands for seal crews before the storm.
reasons.aco: Our helpers handed over to the engineers.
reasons.mca: Loyalists wasted on pump duty.
reasons.riw: Unpaid volunteers doing union maintenance work.
reasons.fam: At least the Earth-born get no stunners.

answers.text: Refuse the League; let Tube Watches guard the tube
answers.sub: Mars-born youth patrols keep the tube. Dome 1 keeps police.

reasons.fam: Our own youth guard our own locks.
reasons.cas: The tube districts get a say in their policing.
reasons.aco: Our posts handed to a Free Arcadia militia.
reasons.mca: The governor blesses a separatist militia.
reasons.upa: Geneva's hold on the tube weakens.

answers.gripWhy: Policing passes to the block committees.

situations.title: Clear the Pad Field
situations.question: Will you send the Constabulary to secure the Pad Field for the Marines?
situations.body: The fleet is two months out. The Marine commander wants a cleared Pad Field, the landing ground, and fuelled landers. Free Arcadia vows to sit on the pads. Director Wen warns that a Marine base facing west ends Utopia's overland supply convoys.

answers.text: Seal the Pad Field for the Marine landing
answers.sub: Police hold the gates and remove protesters from the pads.

reasons.mca: The Marines land on a cleared field, on schedule.
reasons.aco: We hold the gates, not the tube committees.
reasons.fam: Marines stepping onto pads cleared by police.
reasons.upa: A Marine base on our western flank.
reasons.cas: Troops land before the Assembly has voted.

answers.gripWhy: Police clear the pads by force.

answers.text: Leave the pads to the tube committees
answers.sub: Block committees hold the field. The Marines must negotiate to land.

reasons.fam: Arcadia decides who sets foot on its ground.
reasons.cas: The Marines must deal with the settlers first.
reasons.mca: Charter troops held hostage at their own pads.
reasons.aco: Our gates surrendered to a blockade.
reasons.hac: Our cargo stuck in orbit behind a sit-in.

answers.gripWhy: The pads pass to the street.

answers.text: Hand the field to Directorate pad controllers
answers.sub: Engineers schedule the landings. No troops on the gates.

reasons.hsd: Landings go by load table, not by politics.
reasons.upa: No Marine base, only a landing schedule.
reasons.mca: Geneva's troops wait for an engineer's time slot.
reasons.aco: Our gates go to engineers in grey.
reasons.fam: The Marines still land, just more politely.

situations.title: Concord of the Landing
situations.question: Will you sponsor the Exchange's Concord of the Landing?
situations.body: Exchange families drafted a deal called the Concord of the Landing. Arcadia would become a dominion: self-ruling under a revised Charter. Helion-Ares bonds would be paid in full, ₵12 of debt. The Assembly keeps the levy, the local tax. Geneva keeps the flag and the rescue guarantee.

answers.text: Sponsor the Concord and honour the bonds
answers.sub: Dominion status, Exchange seats, and Helion-Ares paid.

reasons.lme: Our families write the terms of the new order.
reasons.hac: Every bond honoured, in writing.
reasons.cas: Dominion gives the Assembly real powers.
reasons.fam: Half a nation, with the bondholders on top.
reasons.riw: Our ice pays Helion-Ares's interest forever.
reasons.mca: A revised Charter we did not draft.

answers.text: Reject it. Only Geneva revises the Charter.
answers.sub: The Charter stands until the Review Commission rules.

reasons.mca: The Charter is revised in Geneva, not in the arcade.
reasons.aco: One chain of command, unchanged.
reasons.lme: Our compromise thrown out unread.
reasons.cas: Our powers stay on Geneva's leash.
reasons.hac: No deal to lock in our bonds.

answers.text: Demand bond cuts and the ice held in common
answers.sub: A Concord only if workers' councils get the ice plants.

reasons.riw: The ice belongs to those who mine it.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice stays in Arcadian hands.
reasons.hac: Our plant seized under a peace deal.
reasons.lme: Our Concord turned into a union charter.
reasons.mca: Refusing debts sets a precedent across the system.

situations.title: One Key for Every Lock
situations.question: Will you give the Directorate the master key to every airlock?
situations.body: The Directorate wants one master key over all 9,000 lock codes before the fleet arrives. Today the Constabulary holds the public locks. Tube block committees hold their own. The Control Ring, the Directorate's control room, says split codes kill people in a breach.

answers.text: Put every lock under the Directorate master key
answers.sub: The Control Ring overrides every code. Police and committees lose theirs.

reasons.hsd: A breach answered in seconds, from one board.
reasons.upa: Engineers holding the locks keep the colony orderly.
reasons.aco: The Control Ring takes our lock codes.
reasons.fam: The engineers can seal the tube at will.
reasons.cas: Every door in the colony behind one unelected key.

answers.gripWhy: One office controls every door.

answers.text: Give the codes to the Constabulary under Charter seal
answers.sub: Lock Security holds every code and answers to Dome 1.

reasons.aco: Locks are security, and security is ours.
reasons.mca: Charter police hold the doors when the Marines land.
reasons.hsd: Police holding codes they cannot engineer.
reasons.fam: Constables can lock our blocks shut.
reasons.riw: The police can seal the halls during a picket.

answers.gripWhy: Police take every door code.

answers.text: Let block and shift councils keep their codes
answers.sub: Elected committees hold their locks. The Control Ring can only watch.

reasons.riw: Crews hold the doors they maintain.
reasons.fam: No one locks the tube from Dome 1.
reasons.hsd: Split codes in a breach mean dead settlers.
reasons.aco: Committees keep codes the police cannot override.
reasons.mca: Geneva's governor holds no keys to her own colony.

answers.gripWhy: The locks stay with elected councils.

situations.title: Two Moons on Dome 1
situations.question: Will you raise the two-moon banner on the Dome 1 mast?
situations.body: Free Arcadia sewed its banner from old spacesuit fabric: rust red, with two moons. It wants it beside the Charter flag at the Reckoning, when the fleet arrives. The Commissioner says any second flag means a second authority. The Charter members of the Assembly threaten to walk out.

answers.text: Raise the two-moon banner beside the Charter flag
answers.sub: Arcadian colours fly on Dome 1 for the Reckoning.

reasons.fam: Our banner on the governor's own mast.
reasons.cas: The self-government bloc wins its symbol.
reasons.mca: A second flag is a second authority.
reasons.aco: Officers made to salute a separatist rag.
reasons.upa: Arcadia shows it does not belong only to Geneva.

answers.text: Fly the union glove banner for the crews instead
answers.sub: A workers' flag, neither Geneva's nor the nation's.

reasons.riw: The people who make the air get the mast.
reasons.fam: Our banner pushed aside for the union's.
reasons.hsd: A strike flag over the Control Ring.
reasons.mca: Any flag beside the Charter's is defiance.
reasons.aco: The picket banner flying on Dome 1.

answers.text: Fly Exchange and Helion-Ares colours to welcome the fleet
answers.sub: A trade banner for the landing, and no flag fight.

reasons.lme: Our tower logo greets 3,100 new customers.
reasons.hac: Our sunburst welcomes our own cargo.
reasons.fam: Company logos in place of our nation.
reasons.mca: Company colours where only the Charter should fly.
reasons.riw: The bosses' logo over the crews' colony.

situations.title: The Final Reading
situations.question: Governor, will you sign the Declaration, veto it, or stall it?
situations.body: The Declaration of Self-Government reaches its final vote. The bill passed its second reading 33 to 17. Director Wen of Utopia Planitia stands ready to recognise it. The fleet reaches orbit within days with 400 Charter Marines aboard.

answers.text: Sign the Declaration of Self-Government
answers.sub: Ares Landing governs itself. Charter law ends in Arcadia.

reasons.fam: Arcadia is a nation, signed by the governor.
reasons.cas: The Assembly becomes a sovereign parliament.
reasons.upa: A free neighbour leaning west, not to Geneva.
reasons.mca: Secession on our watch, by our own appointee.
reasons.aco: Our oath to the Charter made void.
reasons.hac: Our bonds now owed by a rebel colony.

answers.gripWhy: Power passes to the elected Assembly.

answers.text: Use the Charter veto
answers.sub: The Declaration dies. Renewal is the only path left.

reasons.mca: The Charter holds, and no precedent is set.
reasons.aco: Clear authority when the Marines land.
reasons.cas: Thirty-three votes thrown away by Geneva's pen.
reasons.fam: The governor kills the nation at birth.
reasons.upa: Geneva's hold on Arcadia is restored.

answers.gripWhy: You override the elected Assembly.

answers.text: Send it to a Directorate reserve audit first
answers.sub: No vote until engineers certify the colony can breathe alone.

reasons.hsd: Independence must pass the gauges first.
reasons.upa: An orderly, engineered handover suits us.
reasons.cas: Our sovereignty held hostage by an engineers' board.
reasons.fam: The engineers stall our freedom with paperwork.
reasons.mca: An audit, not a veto, keeps secession alive.

situations.title: Card Them on the Pads
situations.question: Will you make the 3,100 newcomers join the union from their first day?
situations.body: The fleet carries 3,100 settlers, most on Helion-Ares labour contracts. The RIWU, the ice workers' union, has 2,900 members. It wants every newcomer signed up on the landing pads. Helion-Ares says its contracts forbid it. The Exchange wants them free to hire.

answers.text: Sign every newcomer into the union on landing
answers.sub: Union shift rules bind all 3,100 from their first day.

reasons.riw: The union doubles to 6,000 before they unpack.
reasons.fam: Newcomers tied to the colony, not to Geneva.
reasons.hac: Our contracts torn up on the pads.
reasons.lme: No hiring without the union's permission.
reasons.hsd: Shift rules set by the union hall, not the board.

answers.text: Let the newcomers sign any contract they like
answers.sub: Open hiring. The Exchange and Helion-Ares bid for workers.

reasons.lme: 3,100 hands to hire at market rates.
reasons.hac: Our contracts stand as signed on Earth.
reasons.riw: Cheap strikebreakers dumped onto our ice fields.
reasons.fam: Newcomers tied to Earth firms, not to Arcadia.
reasons.cas: Settlers choose their own work.

answers.text: Assign newcomers by the Directorate skills register
answers.sub: Engineers post each settler where the reserves need hands.

reasons.hsd: Labour goes where the reserve log says.
reasons.upa: Planned labour, as it should be.
reasons.riw: Conscripted crews working outside union rules.
reasons.lme: No one left for us to hire.
reasons.hac: Our contract workers moved around by bureaucrats.

answers.gripWhy: Settlers are posted to jobs by order.

situations.title: A Charter for Sale
situations.question: Will you back Helion-Ares's offer to buy the Charter outright?
situations.body: Helion-Ares offers to take over the Arcadia Charter and run the colony as a company concession. In return it would cancel the ₵12 bond debt. The Exchange is split: the big landing-pad families say yes, the arcade shops say no. Geneva has not answered.

answers.text: Back the company takeover and the debt relief
answers.sub: Helion-Ares holds the Charter. The ₵12 debt is cancelled.

reasons.hac: We own the colony we built.
reasons.lme: The debt is gone, and the pad families get rich.
reasons.mca: Geneva's Charter sold off like cargo.
reasons.riw: The bosses become the government.
reasons.fam: Arcadia sold to an Earth company.
reasons.cas: The Assembly would answer to a board of directors.

answers.text: Refuse, and claim the ice plant for the crews
answers.sub: No sale. The union council takes over Helion-Ares's plant.

reasons.riw: The plant goes to the crews who run it.
reasons.fam: Earth money out of Arcadian ice.
reasons.hac: Our plant seized. Our red line crossed.
reasons.lme: Today the plant, tomorrow our greenhouse decks.
reasons.mca: Seizing Earth property invites lawsuits in Geneva.

situations.title: Oath in Orbit
situations.question: Will you take the renewed Charter oath aboard the flagship?
situations.body: The Commissioner wants you in orbit on the fleet's flagship. Charter Hymn, twelve stars, the oath of the renewed Charter. The Assembly has not yet voted. The shuttle leaves the Pad Field in two sols.

answers.text: Fly up and take the oath before the vote
answers.sub: You are the renewed Charter's governor before Arcadia speaks.

reasons.mca: Renewal sworn before anyone can vote it down.
reasons.aco: The chain of command, sworn in blue.
reasons.hac: Continuity keeps our bonds safe.
reasons.cas: Our vote decided in orbit before we sit.
reasons.fam: The governor kneels to Geneva over our heads.

answers.text: Refuse; swear in the tube or not at all
answers.sub: Any oath waits for the Assembly vote, on Arcadian ground.

reasons.fam: The governor's feet stay on Arcadian rock.
reasons.cas: The Assembly votes before anyone swears.
reasons.mca: Our appointee snubs the Charter's flagship.
reasons.aco: No clear oath to stand behind.
reasons.upa: Ares Landing will not kneel to Geneva.

callbacks.title: Shift C Stopped
callbacks.question: Will you uphold your inspector's halt at Ice Field 7?
callbacks.body: You gave RIWU inspectors the power to stop a shift. They used it. Shift C at Ice Field 7 is halted: dust in 31 suit seals. Helion-Ares counts two lost tankers. The Directorate wants the halt lifted by margin order.

answers.text: Uphold the halt until seals are replaced.
answers.sub: New seals first, tankers later.

reasons.riw: The governor keeps the word given to our crews.
reasons.fam: Mars-born lungs come before Earth bonds.
reasons.hac: Two tankers lost to a union stop order.
reasons.hsd: The ice line drops while union doctors decide.

answers.text: Lift it by Directorate margin order.
answers.sub: Margins override inspectors when reserves are tight.

reasons.hsd: The margin board has the last word, as it should.
reasons.hac: The tankers roll and the quota stands.
reasons.riw: Our inspectors' power was worth nothing after all.
reasons.fam: Dome 1 breaks its promise to the crews.

answers.gripWhy: A union safety order overridden by decree.

callbacks.title: Helion-Ares Strikes Back
callbacks.question: You froze the quota. Will you now let Helion-Ares cut Field 7 shifts?
callbacks.body: You froze Helion-Ares's 15 percent quota rise at Ice Field 7. The Consortium now wants to cut contract shifts there. The RIWU says Field 7 can run without the Consortium.

answers.text: Hold the freeze; union crews run Field 7
answers.sub: Crews set their own shifts. Helion-Ares buys the output.

reasons.riw: The field is run by those who dig it.
reasons.hac: Our concession run by the union we fought.
reasons.lme: Union control of ice prices threatens the arcade.
reasons.hsd: Steady tankers matter more than who signs shifts.

answers.text: Bind Field 7 output to colony use first
answers.sub: Arcadian needs come first. Exports take what remains.

reasons.fam: Arcadian ice for Arcadians, written into order.
reasons.cas: The colony's resource answers to the colony.
reasons.hac: Our export contracts subordinated to Areanist slogans.
reasons.mca: Ice withheld from Earth is a step to secession.
reasons.riw: Our ice serves our people before bondholders.

callbacks.title: Valdivia's Cell
callbacks.question: You jailed Valdivia. The tube will not quiet. Will you release him?
callbacks.body: You signed the Article 19 warrant, and Valdivia sits in a Dome 1 cell. The Dustline plays harmonica laments for him nightly. Petitions fill the Assembly's box.

answers.text: Release Valdivia on the Assembly's petition
answers.sub: He walks free pending trial. Charges stand.
answers.gripWhy: A jailed dissident freed by political petition.

reasons.fam: Our founder home in the tube.
reasons.cas: The chamber's petition carries real weight.
reasons.aco: Our arrest undone. Officers look foolish.
reasons.mca: A secessionist freed to broadcast again.

answers.text: Release him into RIWU block-council surety
answers.sub: Union councils guarantee his conduct until trial.
answers.gripWhy: Custody passed to workers' councils.

reasons.riw: The union's councils trusted with public order.
reasons.fam: Free, and bound to the union, not Dome 1.
reasons.aco: Union stewards as jailers make a mockery of law.
reasons.mca: Charter custody handed to a trade union.
reasons.hsd: Union and Areanists aligned is trouble for the plants.

callbacks.title: Marines in the Tube
callbacks.question: Your request brought the Marines; will you hand them the tube posts?
callbacks.body: You asked Geneva for 400 Marines. Geneva agreed. Now the Charter Authority wants their landing plan: the Erebus Tube posts under Marine officers. Dustline calls you the governor who sent for the guns.

answers.text: Give the Marines the tube posts
answers.sub: Marine officers take the Erebus Tube; Constabulary guards domes.

reasons.mca: Charter troops where secession breeds.
reasons.aco: Our tube posts handed to Earth soldiers.
reasons.fam: Marines in our homes: the invasion we warned of.
reasons.cas: Members' districts under Marine officers.
reasons.upa: Marines dug in deeper on Mars.

answers.gripWhy: Earth troops posted in the tube.

answers.text: Confine Marines to the Pad Field barracks
answers.sub: Marines never enter the tube without your order.

reasons.fam: The guns stay at the pads, not in the tube.
reasons.cas: The chamber's limits on force respected.
reasons.aco: The tube remains Constabulary ground.
reasons.mca: Geneva's battalion caged by its own governor.
reasons.hac: Marines idle while our plants need guarding.

answers.gripWhy: Earth troops held back from the settlers.

callbacks.title: Deadlock on the Board
callbacks.question: The union seat blocks the board; will you break the deadlock?
callbacks.body: You gave the RIWU a permanent allocation board seat. Its member now vetoes the Exchange's storm power quota and the Directorate's shift plan. Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist has walked out twice. The water line waits on a vote.

answers.text: Back the union vote; the board follows
answers.sub: Union veto stands; allocation follows shift councils.

reasons.riw: The seat means something: workers allocate.
reasons.fam: Councils over Geneva's engineers.
reasons.hsd: Margins held hostage to union votes.
reasons.lme: Our power quota vetoed by the union.
reasons.hac: Shift councils overruling our contracts.

answers.gripWhy: Allocation answers to an elected council.

answers.text: Give the Chief Engineer a casting vote
answers.sub: Margins break ties; union vote stays but can't block.

reasons.hsd: The gauges get the last word again.
reasons.hac: Engineers, not crews, settle allocations.
reasons.upa: Engineers in charge: a partner we understand.
reasons.riw: A seat without a veto is a chair.
reasons.cas: Another body answering to no voter.

callbacks.title: Train 3 Findings
callbacks.question: Governor, who will you hold to account for Train 3?
callbacks.body: The joint inquiry you opened has reported. Train 3's pressure valve was 400 sols past service. Directorate logs signed it off. The RIWU wants its own safety stewards in every plant.

answers.text: Put RIWU safety stewards in every plant
answers.sub: Stewards can halt any train they judge unsafe.

reasons.riw: Crews can stop the next fire before it starts.
reasons.hsd: Union stewards halting certified plant. Margins held hostage.
reasons.hac: Stewards will halt our trains whenever quotas rise.
reasons.fam: Mars-born workers guarding their own air.
reasons.cas: The inquiry's findings acted on. Accountability, in public.

answers.gripWhy: Workers gain power to stop plant by their own judgement.

answers.text: Let the Directorate discipline its own engineers
answers.sub: Signatories demoted; certification rules tightened inside the Ring.

reasons.hsd: We clean our own house, to our own standard.
reasons.upa: A bureau that polices itself. Orderly.
reasons.aco: No union power over plant locks. Good.
reasons.riw: The inquiry named them, and they judge themselves.
reasons.cas: Public findings handed back behind closed doors.

callbacks.title: The Seat Says No
callbacks.question: The union's seat blocks the air trim. Will you overrule it?
callbacks.body: Your Union Seat Bill gave the RIWU a vote on allocation. Now its delegate blocks the Directorate's 6 percent air trim. Oxygen is under the 180-day floor. Haddad-Lindqvist wants the vote overridden.

answers.text: Honour the union's vote
answers.sub: No trim; the board looks for savings elsewhere.

reasons.riw: The seat means something when it says no.
reasons.fam: Settlers' air is not cut on an engineer's word.
reasons.hsd: The margins are given away for a union vote.
reasons.mca: Below the floor and the governor waits on a union.

answers.text: Override it on Directorate certification
answers.sub: The certified margin trumps the board; the trim goes ahead.

reasons.hsd: Gauges outrank votes below the floor.
reasons.aco: A clear decision is easier to enforce.
reasons.riw: Our seat in law is broken on first use.
reasons.cas: Assembly law is overridden by engineers.

answers.gripWhy: A legal vote is overridden by decree.

answers.text: Refer the deadlock to the Charter Authority
answers.sub: Geneva rules on the trim over the link.

reasons.mca: Geneva remains the final word on air.
reasons.aco: The chain of command runs up to Geneva.
reasons.riw: Our Arcadian law is sent to Earth for review.
reasons.cas: Our law is handed to Geneva to judge.
reasons.hsd: A twenty-minute link delay on a margin call.

callbacks.title: Suit in Geneva Court
callbacks.question: Helion-Ares has sued. Will you hold the plant or buy out its claim?
callbacks.body: The council has run the Ice Field 7 plant since your order, and output is up. Helion-Ares has filed in an Earth court and struck the plant's spares off the manifest. Exchange brokers offer to buy the Consortium's claim.

answers.text: Hold the plant and refuse the suit
answers.sub: No compensation; spares will come from local fabrication.

reasons.riw: The council keeps what it built and runs.
reasons.fam: Earth courts have no writ in the tube.
reasons.hac: Our plant was stolen and the theft defended.
reasons.lme: Every deed in the colony now looks worthless.

answers.text: Let the Exchange buy out the Consortium's claim
answers.sub: The Exchange holds a paper stake; the council keeps the floor.

reasons.lme: We hold the claim on Arcadia's ice plant.
reasons.hac: Cash for a lost plant beats an endless suit.
reasons.riw: New owners hold paper over our council.
reasons.fam: Earth's claim simply passes to the Exchange.

callbacks.title: Committees Cut Dome 1
callbacks.question: The blocks cut Dome 1's water. Will you back them or the meters?
callbacks.body: You gave the block committees legal force over the meters. Now they vote Dome 1's share down 12 percent to cover tube families. Charter clerks and the medical service queue at dry taps. The Directorate says the cut is lawful but unsafe for the clinic.

answers.text: Back the committees' cut to Dome 1
answers.sub: The law you signed stands; Dome 1 shares the ration.

reasons.riw: Common stock means Dome 1 queues like the rest.
reasons.fam: Dome 1 finally feels what the tube has felt.
reasons.hsd: The clinic margin was never the committees' call.
reasons.mca: Earth citizens rationed by tube committees.
reasons.aco: Our families in Dome 1 pay for your experiment.

answers.text: Restore Directorate metering for Dome 1 lines
answers.sub: Engineers take back the valves for the old modules.

reasons.hsd: Certified figures back where they belong.
reasons.aco: Dome 1 is secure again.
reasons.mca: The Charter's own settlers protected.
reasons.riw: You gave us the law, then took it back.
reasons.fam: Dome 1 gets an exemption; the tube does not.

answers.gripWhy: Committee authority is overridden by decree.

callbacks.title: Helion Field
callbacks.question: The buyer wants Ice Field 7 renamed. Will you let it go?
callbacks.body: You sold the berths and names through Helion-Ares. The top bidder wants Ice Field 7 renamed 'Helion Field' and tourist walks past the crews. The RIWU hall sits on that field. Its print shop already has posters up.

answers.text: Keep Ice Field 7's name; crews refuse tours
answers.sub: Refund the bidder; the field stays the union's.

reasons.riw: Ice Field 7 is where we struck; it keeps its name.
reasons.fam: Workers' ground stays Arcadian ground.
reasons.cas: Members wanted public names off the auction.
reasons.hac: A broken contract with our best buyer.
reasons.lme: Refunds wreck the Exchange's word with Earth.

answers.text: Rename it Helion Field and pay a tour bonus
answers.sub: Contract honoured; crews get credits for the walkways.

reasons.lme: Contracts honoured keep Earth money coming.
reasons.hac: Our name on the field that strikes against us.
reasons.mca: Earth investment in Arcadia ties it to home.
reasons.riw: A bonus does not buy the name of our hall.
reasons.fam: Corporate logos over the ice we call ours.

callbacks.title: League Patrol Fires Stunners
callbacks.question: Will you rein in the Charter League you armed?
callbacks.body: You armed the Charter League. Last sol a League patrol stunned three Mars-born youths at the Erebus locks. Tube committees shut two inner locks. The RIWU threatens to down tools.

answers.text: Disarm the League; shift councils staff the locks
answers.sub: League stunners withdrawn; elected crews guard the inner locks.

reasons.riw: Crews, not vigilantes, hold the tube locks.
reasons.fam: The League's stunners are gone.
reasons.aco: Our auxiliaries disarmed by the union.
reasons.mca: Loyalists punished for guarding the Charter.
reasons.cas: Order without a settler militia.

answers.gripWhy: Armed loyalists stand down.

answers.text: Fold the League into Directorate lock maintenance
answers.sub: Stunners into store; members repair seals under engineers.

reasons.hsd: Four hundred hands for the seal crews.
reasons.upa: Militias tamed into maintenance, as is proper.
reasons.aco: Our auxiliaries handed to the Control Ring.
reasons.fam: Disarmed, at least.
reasons.riw: Volunteers doing union maintenance unpaid.

answers.text: Pay the youths' families from an Exchange fund
answers.sub: Compensation settles it; the League keeps its stunners.

reasons.lme: A quiet settlement keeps the arcade open.
reasons.aco: The League stays armed.
reasons.fam: Our youth stunned, and blood money paid.
reasons.riw: Credits instead of disarming the gangs.
reasons.cas: The families get something, fast.

callbacks.title: The Concord Bill Splits
callbacks.question: Will you push your Concord through, or bend it toward the tube?
callbacks.body: You sponsored the Concord of the Landing. The Exchange bench drafted it as a bill. The self-government bloc says dominion is a leash with gold piping. Helion-Ares wants the bond clause untouched.

answers.text: Keep the bond clause and whip the Exchange bench
answers.sub: The Concord passes as drafted; Helion-Ares is paid in full.

reasons.lme: Our draft becomes law, word for word.
reasons.hac: The bond clause survives intact.
reasons.cas: The governor whips our votes for the arcade.
reasons.fam: A leash with gold piping.
reasons.riw: Our ice mortgaged to Helion-Ares for decades.

answers.text: Add Arcadian citizenship and colony ice ownership
answers.sub: The Mars-born become Arcadians; the ice stays with the colony.

reasons.fam: Arcadians in law, and Arcadian ice.
reasons.cas: The bloc can vote for a real Concord.
reasons.hac: Our export rights written out of the bill.
reasons.lme: Our compromise hijacked by the tube.
reasons.mca: A citizenship that is not Earth's.
